story_updates.headline: Turkiye and Syria sign phosphate and energy deals, tripling power transmission to 800MW
story_updates.summary: Turkish and Syrian ministers signed a phosphate memorandum in Damascus and agreed infrastructure due within weeks that will roughly triple cross-border electricity transmission capacity to more than 800 megawatts. Turkey's state oil company TPAO and private Turkish firms signed energy agreements clearing exploration across Syrian onshore and offshore blocks — among the most concrete foreign energy commitments since the change of government. Turkey is Damascus's principal economic lifeline, which is also the lever through which Ankara shapes Syrian policy on the Kurdish file.

story_updates.headline: SDF dissolves itself and merges into the Syrian army, ending Kurdish de facto autonomy
story_updates.summary: Mazloum Abdi announced on 25 August that the Syrian Democratic Forces had completed integration and ceased to exist as an independent force, calling it the start of a transition "from the battlefields to the fields of construction". Military units fold into the army under the Defence Ministry and affiliated security forces into the Interior Ministry; Abdi becomes a presidential adviser and Kurdish commanders take senior posts. Unresolved: whether fighters answer to Damascus or to local commands, where they deploy, the status of the YPJ women's units, and guarantees on Kurdish language, education and local policing. Reporting indicates fewer than half of SDF fighters had actually been absorbed.

story_updates.headline: Analysis: SDF integration is a win for al-Sharaa but 'exists largely on paper'
story_updates.summary: Christian Brakel of the Heinrich Boll Foundation's Beirut office tells DW the dissolution is a substantial win for al-Sharaa's drive to concentrate authority in Damascus, but that a unified army is still more true on paper than on the ground: many SDF fighters are not yet absorbed, the mechanics of integration are unclear, and parts of the existing army — implicated in the Sweida and coastal massacres — are not under full central discipline. He notes the outcome is worse for the SDF than the March 2025 deal, follows the US pivot from the SDF toward Damascus under Turkish pressure, and leaves Kurdish cultural and political rights, not autonomy, as the live question — a plausible source of new grievance if the schooling and constitutional guarantees fall short.

story_updates.headline: The world comes to New York: What’s at stake at UN General Assembly high-level week
story_updates.summary: Each September, New York becomes the centre of global diplomacy as presidents, prime ministers, ministers and diplomats from around the world gather at United Nations Headquarters.

story_updates.headline: AI, climate and conflicts top Guterres’s agenda ahead of General Assembly
story_updates.summary: Ahead of the UN General Assembly’s high-level week, Secretary-General António Guterres said the world had entered “an era of deep uncertainty” and urged governments to embrace international cooperation to address global threats.

story_updates.headline: Why the UN General Assembly still matters
story_updates.summary: More than eight decades on from its founding, the UN General Assembly remains the place where the UN’s 193 Member States come together to debate the defining challenges of the day, from war and peace – to development, climate change and human rights.

story_updates.headline: Lula opens the debate: UN credibility "never lower", Gaza a genocide, Brazil "in no one's backyard"
story_updates.summary: Opening for the tenth time, Lula blamed the veto-bound Security Council for UN paralysis, accused the Netanyahu government of genocide in Gaza, and rejected renewed US "hegemonic temptations" in Latin America.

story_updates.headline: Trump weighs Iran deal or "annihilating the Islamic Republic"; touts Venezuela, Greenland bases, UN cuts
story_updates.summary: Trump said he faces "a big decision" on Iran, expects a deal after the US elections, hailed Maduro's capture and a Venezuelan oil deal, announced major bases in Greenland, and urged states to quit the "rogue" ICC.

story_updates.headline: Macron warns of a return to "the law of the jungle" and a new order of impunity
story_updates.summary: Macron said the Geneva Conventions are being dismantled from El Fasher to Gaza, warned that regime-change interventions bring chaos, and proposed a double moratorium on strikes in Ukraine.

story_updates.headline: Erdoğan calls Gaza "the most shameful concentration camp of our time"; "the world is bigger than five"
story_updates.summary: Erdoğan condemned a "genocidal mindset" in the West Bank and highlighted Türkiye's defence alliance with Saudi Arabia and Pakistan over the Gulf war. King Abdullah and Qatar's Emir echoed calls to restrain Israel.

story_updates.headline: Time to accept ‘hard truths’ so trust can be rebuilt: General Assembly President
story_updates.summary: The UN’s survival for 80 years is not, by itself, proof of success, and now, the institution must confront painful truths if it hopes to rebuild public trust, said Khalilur Rahman, president of the General Assembly’s 81st session on Tuesday.

story_updates.headline: Diplomacy is the way to address global challenges, Brazil tells General Assembly
story_updates.summary: Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva told the General Assembly on Tuesday that the UN needs to become a “temple of peace” once again, as it confronts one of the most critical periods in its 80-year history.

story_updates.headline: Trump defends military action against Iran, Venezuela, and calls for rebrand of AI
story_updates.summary: US President Donald Trump used his address to the UN General Assembly on Tuesday to defend recent military action against Iran, urging countries to maintain economic pressure on Tehran – and declaring that he now faces a choice between making a deal, or taking far more drastic steps.

story_updates.headline: Zelenskyy: Putin paying "248 people for every kilometre" in his Donetsk land grab
story_updates.summary: Zelenskyy said Russia lost 248,964 troops in eight months, accused North Korea of sending troops and drones, and warned of Russian designs on Moldova, Poland and the Baltics.

story_updates.headline: Pezeshkian: US and Israel killed Iran's supreme leader; "Israel kills but Iran is sanctioned"
story_updates.summary: Iran's president said Iran only defended itself, insisted on its right to peaceful nuclear technology, and denounced double standards over Israel's arsenal and actions in Gaza.

story_updates.headline: Cyprus calls Erdoğan's sovereignty remarks "hypocrisy of the highest form"
story_updates.summary: Christodoulides told Erdoğan to "first apply" the Charter he quotes, over the Turkish occupation of northern Cyprus, and urged talks on a bizonal, bicommunal federation to resume.

story_updates.headline: United Kingdom announces action on disinformation and global AI standards
story_updates.summary: The United Kingdom will fight disinformation at home and abroad, and work to ensure global safety standards for artificial intelligence (AI), new Prime Minister Andy Burnham said on Monday evening in his first address to the United Nations General Assembly.

story_updates.headline: Syria begins ‘new phase of revival’, President Al-Sharaa tells General Assembly
story_updates.summary: Syrian President Ahmad Al-Sharaa told the UN General Assembly on Wednesday that his country “is rising” on many levels, thanks to the strength of its people.

story_updates.headline: At UN, Pezeshkian turns terrorism accusation back on Iran’s critics
story_updates.summary: President Masoud Pezeshkian opened his General Assembly address with a direct rebuttal to US President Donald Trump, who a day earlier had branded Iran the “number one sponsor of terror.”

story_updates.headline: UN’s ‘sacred covenant has been broken’, Argentina’s Milei tells General Assembly
story_updates.summary: Argentine President Javier Milei told the General Assembly on Wednesday that the UN has broken the “sacred covenant” on which it was founded, failing at what it was meant to do – while excelling at things beyond its remit.

story_updates.headline: Equality ‘ends at the doors of the Security Council’, Kenya’s Ruto tells General Assembly
story_updates.summary: Kenyan President William Ruto told the General Assembly on Wednesday that the sovereign equality the UN proclaims is contradicted by its own structures, urging Member States to reform the Security Council and an international financial system “built for another age”.

story_updates.headline: Netanyahu to walkout: "Israel didn't commit genocide, it prevented genocide"
story_updates.summary: Netanyahu called striking Iran's nuclear sites "one of the easiest decisions", named Trump Israel's greatest partner, and accused Qatar, Türkiye and NYC Mayor Mamdani. Qatar, Türkiye and Iran all used rights of reply to answer him.

story_updates.headline: Abbas, speaking by video after visa denial, warns "do not allow another Nakba"
story_updates.summary: Abbas said a "genocidal war" and settlement drive toward "Greater Israel" threaten Palestinians' existence, and urged Trump to honour his pledge to block annexation.

story_updates.headline: Gulf states catalogue Iranian attacks: Kuwait, Bahrain demand Hormuz reopen without Iranian fees
story_updates.summary: Kuwait's crown prince and Bahrain (citing some 7,000 attacks on the GCC and Jordan) condemned Iranian strikes on civilian infrastructure and its use of Hormuz as a bargaining chip.

story_updates.headline: The Takeaway: UN General Assembly debate Day 2
story_updates.summary: This edition of UN News's The Takeaway recaps key highlghts at the UN General Assembly on Wednesday, including focus on the war in Ukraine and a renewed push by African countries for Security Council reform.

story_updates.headline: ‘Peace remains only a promise’ for millions in eastern DR Congo, General Assembly hears
story_updates.summary: The Prime Minister of the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) cautioned against growing global demand for “blood-stained minerals” in the rush to net-zero, in her speech to the UN General Assembly.

story_updates.headline: Palestinian existence under threat, Abbas tells UN, warning of ‘another Nakba’
story_updates.summary: Israeli policies now threaten “the very life and existence of the Palestinian people on their homeland”, Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas told the UN General Assembly on Thursday, urging the world not to allow “another Nakba”.

story_updates.headline: Israeli leader at UN: ‘We’re going to win. We have no other choice’
story_updates.summary: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu used his address to the UN General Assembly to defend Israel’s strikes against Iran as a matter of national survival and described the violence in the West Bank as the work of a few “juvenile delinquents” and rejected accusations of genocide in Gaza as “the greatest lie of the century.”

story_updates.headline: Yemen’s path to stability depends on restoring the state, Leadership Council vice-president tells UN
story_updates.summary: The Vice-President of Yemen’s Presidential Leadership Council, Abdullah Al-Alimi Bawazir, told the UN General Assembly on Thursday that his Government had engaged “responsibly and positively” with regional and international peace initiatives and made significant concessions to end the suffering of the Yemeni people.

story_updates.headline: Sharif: any diversion of Indus waters "will be treated as an act of war"; thanks Trump for averting war
story_updates.summary: Pakistan's prime minister demanded a Kashmir plebiscite and called India's suspension of the Indus Waters Treaty illegal. That night India and Pakistan traded rights of reply over terrorism and Kashmir.

story_updates.headline: Lebanon refuses to be "a bargaining chip" in others' wars
story_updates.summary: Nawaf Salam said weapons must be in state hands only, sought Israel's withdrawal via US-mediated talks, and backed Gulf states against Iranian attacks.

story_updates.headline: Australia urges global cooperation on climate, AI checks and international law
story_updates.summary: Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese underlined the need for countries to work together to address the climate crisis, emerging technologies such as AI, and the breakdown of international rules, at the United Nations General Assembly on Thursday.

story_updates.headline: Nepal PM urges climate justice after ‘Himalayan tsunami’ devastates country
story_updates.summary: Nepal’s Prime Minister Balendra Shah brought a stark warning from the Himalayas to the UN General Assembly on Thursday, saying catastrophic floods that killed at least 1,400 people in his country laid bare the human cost of climate change, and the failure of the international system to protect those least responsible for it.

story_updates.headline: Tuvalu urges decisive global action as rising seas threaten its future
story_updates.summary: Climate change remains the greatest existential threat to Tuvalu, Prime Minister Feleti Teo told the UN General Assembly on Friday, warning that the pace and scale of international action are still falling far short of what vulnerable island nations need.

story_updates.headline: Pakistan’s Sharif warns any diversion of Indus waters will be ‘treated as an act of war’
story_updates.summary: Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif told the UN General Assembly on Friday that any attempt by India to stop, impede or divert Pakistan’s share of the Indus River waters “will be treated as an act of war”.

story_updates.headline: Haiti at ‘watershed moment’, Prime Minister tells UN, urging full backing for security force
story_updates.summary: Haiti is at a “watershed moment” in its struggle against gang violence and needs sustained international support alongside stronger national security institutions, Prime Minister Alix Didier Fils-Aimé told the UN General Assembly on Friday.

story_updates.headline: Lavrov: a "Western minority" clings to 500 years of privilege; condemns Maduro's capture and Khamenei's killing
story_updates.summary: Lavrov said the special military operation's goals "will be achieved", accused the US of creating a "Russophobic regime in Kyiv", and backed Brazil and India (not Germany or Japan) for permanent Council seats.

story_updates.headline: China's Han Zheng: "the world wants peace, not war"; rejects bloc confrontation and decoupling
story_updates.summary: China promoted its four global initiatives, backed "Palestinians governing Palestine", pledged a constructive role "in its own way" on Ukraine, and demanded an end to the Cuba blockade.

story_updates.headline: Jaishankar: distant wars punish bystanders amid a "weaponization of everything"
story_updates.summary: India urged de-escalation in the Gulf and an end to the Ukraine war, warned of terrorism with a pointed message to Pakistan, and defended every nation's right to its own AI models.

story_updates.headline: Cuba calls the US fuel blockade an act of war: "Cuba is not a threat. The blockade is."
story_updates.summary: Cuba's foreign minister said Washington's bid to impose peace by force is unrealizable; dozens of Caribbean, African and Latin American states called for the embargo to end during the week.

story_updates.headline: The Takeaway: UN General Assembly debate Day 4
story_updates.summary: From the Caribbean to the Pacific, leaders from small island States demanded climate justice, ocean protection and greater solidarity at the UN General Assembly on Friday.  They warned that rising seas are already redrawing national boundaries, while the ripple effects of faraway wars are being felt on their shores. This edition of The Takeaway summarizes key points made during the fourth...

story_updates.headline: ‘Safeguard the postwar order,’ China tells UN General Assembly
story_updates.summary: China's Vice President, Han Zheng, urged the world to defend the postwar international order on Saturday, telling the UN General Assembly that geopolitical conflicts, widening development gaps and mounting global challenges make multilateralism more urgent than ever.

story_updates.headline: Lavrov issues call for new Eurasian ‘security architecture’
story_updates.summary: Russia's Foreign Minister, Sergey Lavrov, accused Western countries of destabilising the world through “force and double standards” in his address to the UN General Assembly on Saturday, vowing that Moscow's “special military operation” in Ukraine would be “carried through to the end.”

story_updates.headline: Cuba warns against ‘law of the jungle’ as Foreign Minister denounces US pressure
story_updates.summary: Cuba’s Foreign Minister warned the UN General Assembly on Saturday that escalating military and economic pressure in Latin America and the Caribbean was threatening international law, while accusing the United States of intensifying a decades-long campaign to isolate and weaken his country.

story_updates.headline: Canada urges stronger partnerships as global order faces ‘rupture’
story_updates.summary: Canada’s Foreign Minister Anita Anand warned the UN General Assembly on Saturday that the international order has entered an era of profound disruption, calling for stronger multilateral cooperation and new partnerships as major powers increasingly turn away from global economic integration.

story_updates.headline: Debate closes with clashes: China and DPRK vs Japan, Iran vs UAE, Sudan calls UAE "country of evil"
story_updates.summary: In the final right-of-reply session China and the DPRK accused Japan of "neo-militarism" and defended the Charter's enemy-state clauses; China and the Philippines clashed over the 2016 South China Sea award; Iran warned neighbours hosting US forces of a "devastating response" while the UAE called three Gulf islands occupied; and Sudan and the UAE traded accusations over the RSF and chemical weapons.

story_updates.headline: DPRK tells UN its nuclear status is irreversible, denounces US "tyranny"
story_updates.summary: Vice-Foreign Minister Kim Son Gyong said the US is turning its alliance with Japan and South Korea into an offensive bloc aimed at the DPRK, credited Pyongyang's nuclear deterrent with preventing war on the peninsula, and said there is "no going back" on its status as a nuclear-weapons state.

story_updates.headline: Sudan says US denied al-Burhan a visa; demands RSF be dismantled and its sponsors named
story_updates.summary: Foreign Minister Mohieldin Salim said he spoke because the host country denied General al-Burhan a visa. He called the world's silence on the Rapid Support Forces "a betrayal of the civilian victims" and said widening the Darfur arms embargo to all of Sudan would hand the militia victory.

story_updates.headline: UAE rejects Iran's "occupation" of three Gulf islands, backs Trump's Gaza plan
story_updates.summary: Minister of State Khalifa Shaheen Al Marar called for settling the Greater Tunb, Lesser Tunb and Abu Musa dispute by talks or the ICJ, stressed freedom of navigation, cited UAE mediation of Russia-Ukraine prisoner exchanges, and backed full implementation of the Gaza plan including Israeli withdrawal and Hamas disarmament.

story_updates.headline: LIVE: World leaders take stock of global fight against racism
story_updates.summary: World leaders met in the General Assembly Monday to assess how far the world has come in combating racism and how far it still has to go. The Durban Declaration and Programme of Action, the most comprehensive framework of its kind, seeks to acknowledge historical injustices, dismantle inequalities and build societies grounded in dignity, equality and justice for all.

story_updates.headline: Sudan tells UN: No imposed solutions to country’s conflict

story_updates.summary: In the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), UN health teams and partners are still racing to contain the rapidly expanding Ebola outbreak, despite ongoing insecurity in eastern areas where the virus has taken hold. As of 19 July, the DRC Government has recorded 2,423 confirmed cases, including 967 deaths and 469 recoveries.

story_updates.headline: Security Council LIVE: Spotlight on Syria as Guterres heads to Damascus
story_updates.summary: The Security Council discussed the situation on the ground in Syria amid reports of an Israeli attack in occupied territory and of a multi-national oil pipeline to counter the closure of the critical Strait of Hormuz – still the focus of the ongoing US-Iran war. The meeting follows UN independent investigators’ findings that security conditions remain fragile in the south as António Guterres&nb...

story_updates.headline: UN refugee agency reports 144 migrants dead or missing off Mauritanian coast
story_updates.summary: The UN’s refugee agency (UNHCR) reports that 144 migrants attempting to reach Europe are dead or missing due to a series of “tragic maritime incidents” off the coast of Mauritania last week.

story_updates.headline: Global hunger declines again but progress remains uneven across regions
story_updates.summary: Global hunger declined for a third consecutive year in 2025 showing that progress is possible, but gains remain fragile and far too slow to achieve the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) by the 2030 deadline.

story_updates.headline: Guterres calls for stepping up diplomatic efforts to end US-Iran conflict
story_updates.summary: The United Nations again called for restraint as war ramps up in the Middle East, underscoring the need for dialogue and an end to attacks on “vital infrastructure” across the region.

story_updates.headline: Critical minerals: The hidden resources powering the clean energy future
story_updates.summary: Why are critical minerals suddenly at the centre of global politics?

story_updates.headline: Israeli attacks on Gaza intensify amid surge of West Bank settler violence
story_updates.summary: Amid intensified deadly Israeli attacks in Gaza, the UN chief and top officials condemned the killings while a surge violence rocked the West Bank and aid agencies scrambled to help Palestinians.

story_updates.headline: World News in Brief: Sexual violence in DR Congo, deaths in Ukraine and Russia, crime in Southeast Asia
story_updates.summary: Independent UN human rights experts on Tuesday condemned the M23 armed group’s “reign of terror” over territory it controls in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), calling for an end to the Rwanda-backed group’s sexual torture and violence against civilians.

story_updates.headline: ‘Business as usual is a business of death’: UN adopts road safety pledge over US objection
story_updates.summary: The UN General Assembly closed its first ever High-level Meeting on road safety on Tuesday by adopting a sweeping new declaration aimed at halving road deaths by 2030 – over the sole objection of the United States.

story_updates.headline: From lithium to nickel: How the UN is helping countries make the most of critical minerals
story_updates.summary: The world's shift to clean energy is driving huge demand for critical minerals such as lithium, nickel, cobalt and copper.

story_updates.headline: Security Council LIVE: Can critical minerals fuel peace and prosperity instead of conflict?
story_updates.summary: The Security Council met Wednesday in New York to debate critical minerals — the lithium, cobalt and copper powering the clean energy transition. Demand is set to triple by 2030. The question: will this mineral wealth build peace and prosperity, or fund conflict and corruption? Follow live updates throughout the day below and go here for full coverage from across the UN.

story_updates.headline: Deadly Afghanistan floods kill at least 26 as aid agencies race to reach survivors
story_updates.summary: Flash floods have killed at least 26 people across eastern Afghanistan, including 23 in the mountainous province of Nuristan, where homes, markets and roads were swept away and search teams continued looking for people reported missing.

story_updates.headline: Nicaragua continues to weaken political freedoms, UN warns
story_updates.summary: The UN human rights chief Volker Türk on Wednesday condemned new threats from Nicaragua’s co-president Daniel Ortega to hinder civil rights and prevent dissenting individuals and groups from participating in elections.

story_updates.headline: World News in Brief: Aid for Ukraine, drone attacks in Sudan, DR Congo deaths, neurological disorders in the Americas
story_updates.summary: UN partners launched the Winter Response Plan to help 2.1 million people in Ukraine survive another cold season as the country grapples with the on-going Russian invasion.

story_updates.headline: Thousands prevented from returning home to southern Lebanon
story_updates.summary: As months of conflict continue to devastate communities across Lebanon, families are being left without shelter, healthcare and other essential services.

story_updates.headline: Stranded seafarers remain trapped as Hormuz shipping stalls
story_updates.summary: As the Iran-US war continues, the key question remains unanswered about how shipping through the Strait of Hormuz will be managed in future – although the UN has reiterated that charging tolls for safe passage runs contrary to international law.

story_updates.headline: Security Council LIVE: How to turn preventive diplomacy rhetoric into action
story_updates.summary: In the Security Council debate on Thursday on how best to settle disputes between States peacefully, ambassadors provided examples of success and challenges ahead under such themes as effective early warning and how to move from rhetorical support for preventive diplomacy to ensuring more consistent use of its Chapter VI powers under the UN Charter.

story_updates.headline: Gaza’s food gains could unravel without sustained aid, UN warns
story_updates.summary: Food security and child nutrition have improved across the Gaza Strip largely due to a scale-up in humanitarian assistance and commercial traffic, but progress remains fragile and could quickly reverse without sustained access, funding and recovery support.

story_updates.headline: Satellites can now spot methane leaks in real time – but most go unfixed
story_updates.summary: Satellites can now spot major methane leaks from space within days. Yet only 13 per cent of those alerts lead to any response from the governments or companies responsible.

story_updates.headline: World News in Brief: New ECOSOC chief, Secretary-General candidates’ debate, torture in Mali, drowning prevention
story_updates.summary: Amar Bendjama, Permanent Representative of Algeria to the UN, was elected on Thursday to serve as the next president of the UN’s Economic and Social Council (ECOSOC).

story_updates.headline: Iran urged to stop protest-related executions
story_updates.summary: Independent UN human rights investigators on Thursday called for Iran to immediately halt the execution of 10 men who took part in a protest in the central city of Isfahan earlier this year, warning that some of their relatives have already been called for final visits.

story_updates.headline: Syria ‘not alone’ in locating missing persons, tackling displacement
story_updates.summary: Syria is not alone in tackling challenges, including the hundreds of thousands who remain missing during past tumultuous decades, the head of a UN institution said on Thursday as António Guterres departs on his first visit to the country in his current capacity as Secretary-General.

story_updates.headline: In El Obeid, Sudanese women face drones by day, rape by night, to reach water
story_updates.summary: In El Obeid, women and girls now face an impossible choice over something as basic as a bucket of water: risk a drone strike by collecting it in daylight, or risk rape by waiting until dark.

story_updates.headline: Wildfires surge across Europe as Spain and France battle major blazes
story_updates.summary: The amount of land burned by wildfires across Europe has increased by 57 per cent in four years, according to new data from the World Health Organization (WHO) in Europe.

story_updates.headline: Middle East: UN warns against wider escalation after Houthi attacks in the Red Sea
story_updates.summary: As fighting intensifies in the Middle East, the United Nations on Friday warned against further escalation in the US-Iran war and the risks to global shipping amid the fight over control of the Strait of Hormuz.

story_updates.headline: After an Ebola centre was attacked, peacekeepers moved in next door
story_updates.summary: A new mobile UN peacekeeping base in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) has allowed local authorities to continue responding to the fast-moving Ebola outbreak there after violence disrupted the work of medics at a treatment centre set up to contain the spread.

story_updates.headline: ‘Women do not stop giving birth in an emergency’ – one month after Venezuela quakes
story_updates.summary: One month after twin earthquakes rocked Venezuela, thousands of women and girls continue to face difficulty in accessing essential healthcare and protection services, a senior official with the UN reproductive and sexual health agency UNFPA said on Friday.

story_updates.headline: ‘Judges should be superhuman’: The invisible burden behind the bench
story_updates.summary: When conflict erupts, disasters strike or political crises unfold, courts are among the few institutions expected to keep functioning – ensuring the essential rule of law is maintained.

story_updates.headline: Security Council debrief: Race for critical minerals intensifies amidst warnings of conflict
story_updates.summary: The world needs more critical minerals than ever before for electric vehicles, wind turbines, solar panels, batteries and smartphones.

story_updates.headline: International Criminal Court Prosecutor Karim Khan dismissed
story_updates.summary: Member States of the International Criminal Court dismissed its Prosecutor Karim Khan following disciplinary proceedings related to widely reported sexual misconduct allegations at an emergency session at UN Headquarters in New York on Friday.

story_updates.headline: ‘I am somebody’: Street-smart youth take their declaration to the UN
story_updates.summary: When Samantha Richards and Angela Hifume walked into the Hall of Flags at United Nations Headquarters last week, they carried more than a folder of paper. They carried the voices of hundreds of street-connected children who had never expected anyone to listen.

story_updates.headline: UN chief hails Syria’s ‘moment of possibility’ on first visit since fall of Assad regime
story_updates.summary: Syria has an opportunity not only to recover from conflict but to build “a future that is more stable, more inclusive and more prosperous for all Syrians”, UN Secretary-General António Guterres said in Damascus on Saturday as he began a landmark visit to the country.

story_updates.headline: After war took her leg, this Ukrainian gymnast refused to give up
story_updates.summary: When 10-year-old Ukrainian gymnast Sasha Paskal stepped onto the stage in New York's Times Square this week, she carried a message far bigger than her performance.

story_updates.headline: Gaza: Dialysis patients face grueling hospital journey by donkey cart
story_updates.summary: Shortly before sunrise, Palestinian Fathi Hajji begins an arduous thrice weekly journey to Nasser Hospital in Khan Younis in the war-ravaged Gaza Strip.

story_updates.headline: Syria’s hopes for renewal hinge on rebuilding trust, lives and livelihoods
story_updates.summary: A country long known as a meeting point of civilizations, Syria stands once again at a crossroads

story_updates.headline: Security Council LIVE: Briefing on Ukraine as deadly Russian strikes hit cities and ports
story_updates.summary: The UN Security Council met on Monday at Ukraine’s request, following recent large-scale Russian attacks on Kyiv and elsewhere. At least one civilian was killed and more than a dozen wounded in an overnight strike on the capital on 19 July that also damaged homes and civilian infrastructure. Ukrainian authorities described it as one of the largest and most intense attacks since the invasion beg...

story_updates.headline: Cyberattacks and the digital divide are creating new barriers to HIV services
story_updates.summary: Cyberattacks, data breaches, online harassment and other forms of technology-facilitated violence are becoming significant obstacles to HIV prevention and treatment, according to a UNAIDS specialist who says digital security has become inseparable from the fight against the epidemic itself.

story_updates.headline: Conflict and crisis put six World Heritage sites at risk
story_updates.summary: Armed conflict, insecurity and environmental pressures are threatening ancient cities, historic castles and one of the world's greatest wildlife migrations.

story_updates.headline: High prices and funding cuts stall HIV prevention revolution
story_updates.summary: The AIDS epidemic could stage a comeback amid unequal access to breakthrough prevention medicines and a sharp decline in global funding, according to a UN report released on Monday ahead of the opening of the 26th International AIDS Conference in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil.

story_updates.headline: Lebanon: Israeli strikes ‘could amount to international crimes,’ warns Türk
story_updates.summary: UN Human Rights Chief Volker Türk expressed concern about ongoing displacement and destruction caused by Israeli strikes against Lebanon as he concluded a two-day visit to the country on Monday.

story_updates.headline: Guterres: Fast-tracking West Bank outposts is a ‘flagrant violation’ of international law
story_updates.summary: The United Nations continues to monitor developments in the Occupied Palestinian Territory amid rising violence and greater restrictions in the occupied West Bank.

story_updates.headline: 75 years later, the promise to protect refugees faces its greatest test
story_updates.summary: As the world marks the 75th anniversary of the Refugee Convention, the UN refugee agency (UNHCR) has launched a global campaign urging governments, organizations and individuals to renew their commitment to protecting people forced to flee war, violence and persecution.

story_updates.headline: Security Council LIVE: Updates on Gaza, West Bank amid regional tensions
story_updates.summary: Regional tensions are mounting as the US-Iran war continues and a rising number of Israeli attacks are threatening Gaza’s fragile October ceasefire that ended two years of war with Hamas. Security Council members are hearing updates on Tuesday. Join our live coverage.

story_updates.headline: Forced online scams: IOM warns trafficking networks are booming
story_updates.summary: A job advert can hide a criminal network, and a single click can lead to a nightmare. Hundreds of thousands of people are trafficked every year on the promise of legitimate work abroad, only to be held captive and forced into online scam operations.

story_updates.headline: A hijab inspection, a slap, a warning letter: Inside three months of Taliban rule
story_updates.summary: A woman is stopped for buying groceries alone. The shopkeeper who served her is slapped and hauled in for questioning. A teacher is turned away from her own classroom for the wrong cloak.

story_updates.headline: HIV, hepatitis, STI gains at risk as funding falls, WHO warns
story_updates.summary: Years of progress in tackling HIV, viral hepatitis and sexually transmitted infections (STIs) are at risk of stalling, leaving millions of people without access to life-saving prevention, testing and treatment, the World Health Organization (WHO) has warned.

story_updates.headline: Climate alarm ‘blaring from every direction’
story_updates.summary: Climate-driven disasters are reaching “nightmare proportions” due to humanity’s “addiction” to fossil fuels, a top UN official warned on Tuesday.

story_updates.headline: Mount Olympus and D-Day beaches among new World Heritage Sites
story_updates.summary: From the peaks of Mount Olympus in Greece to the shores of the “D-Day” beaches in France, 25 cultural or natural landmarks from across the globe have been newly inscribed on the World Heritage List, updated annually by the UN Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO).

story_updates.headline: Returning Afghans face growing risk of trafficking as crises deepen
story_updates.summary: Afghans returning from neighbouring countries are facing growing risks of human trafficking and exploitation as overlapping humanitarian and economic crises leave many struggling to survive, the UN warned on Thursday.

story_updates.headline: Attacks ‘getting worse’: Deadly Russian strikes hit Ukrainian cities
story_updates.summary: Aid workers and first responders raced to help people across Ukraine after a wave of deadly Russian missile and drone strikes overnight as concerns mounted over military activity near nuclear power plants on Thursday.

story_updates.headline: Wildfires: Prevention is the best defence, UN says
story_updates.summary: The wildfires burning across Europe and North America highlight the urgent need for action now – as climate change, land-use pressures and human activity make severe fires more likely in the future.

story_updates.headline: Middle East crisis: Humanitarian fallout ‘worsening by the day’
story_updates.summary: The humanitarian toll is mounting as fighting continues in the Middle East beyond strikes and counterstrikes between the US and Iran, the UN aid coordination office OCHA warned on Thursday, with civilians increasingly at risk and essential infrastructure disrupted in several countries across the region.

story_updates.headline: The climate pattern putting millions at risk: El Niño explained
story_updates.summary: El Niño is putting millions of lives at risk in eastern and southern Africa but the UN is ensuring that communities are better prepared to deal with its impact.

story_updates.headline: Fear grows as freedoms shrink in Uganda
story_updates.summary: Uganda is experiencing a growing climate of fear as increasing restrictions on fundamental freedoms leave opposition supporters, journalists, human rights defenders and civil society groups at heightened risk of abuse, according to the UN Human Rights Office (OHCHR).

story_updates.headline: Strong El Niño ahead, UN weather agency warns
story_updates.summary: As much of the world faces grapples with above normal temperatures and major rainfall changes, the UN Meteorological Organization (WMO) warned on Friday that El Niño, a powerful climate pattern shaping global weather, will intensify starting next month.

story_updates.headline: Wildfire smoke poses hidden health threat
story_updates.summary: Wildfires are often associated with the destruction they leave behind, but the smoke they produce can pose a serious health threat far beyond the fire zone, the World Health Organization (WHO) has warned.

story_updates.headline: Middle East: Civilian death toll climbs in Gaza, Lebanon and West Bank as UN chief demands ‘the fighting must stop’
story_updates.summary: Violence and civilian casualties are rising across the Middle East – from Israeli airstrikes in Gaza to continued hostilities in Lebanon and the West Bank – UN agencies reported on Friday as the Secretary-General declared “the fighting must stop”.

story_updates.headline: Recovery in Ukraine, one life at a time
story_updates.summary: In classrooms, maternity wards, hospital corridors and local communities across Ukraine, people are rebuilding their lives despite the ongoing war.

story_updates.headline: Trapped by a Facebook job advert, freed by a stranger in a taxi
story_updates.summary: Sofia* was 27, raising her seven-year-old son alone in Venezuela, and running out of options. For years she had distributed personal hygiene products door to door, but as her customers’ finances collapsed, so did her income.

story_updates.headline: DR Congo: New centre opens at heart of record Ebola outbreak
story_updates.summary: New UN-partnered centres will serve eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) as confirmed Ebola cases continued to climb sharply over the weekend in the largest-ever outbreak of the highly contagious disease in the country.

story_updates.headline: Mothers still lack support to breastfeed, UN warns
story_updates.summary: Breastfeeding rates are rising worldwide, but millions of mothers and families still lack the services and protection they need to feed their babies safely, the UN has warned.

story_updates.headline: In Somalia, AI is helping deliver food to hungry families
story_updates.summary: Amid a deepening hunger crisis in Somalia, artificial intelligence (AI) is helping to deliver aid to the people who need it most.

story_updates.headline: Israel violates Lebanese airspace, kills over two dozen in Gaza in weekend strikes
story_updates.summary: Israeli forces reportedly killed more than two dozen Palestinians in Gaza and violated Lebanese airspace more than 100 times over the weekend despite ongoing ceasefire agreements, UN agencies and peacekeepers said on Monday.

story_updates.headline: Drone strikes threaten civilians and aid operations in Sudan
story_updates.summary: Drone strikes are posing deadly risks to civilians in Sudan and hampering humanitarian efforts to reach them as attacks continue to affect conflict-hit areas, the UN aid coordination office OCHA said on Monday.

story_updates.headline: Afghanistan hunger crisis intensifies as millions left without food aid
story_updates.summary: Afghanistan’s dire hunger crisis now affects 14 million people including babies fed on little more than weak tea and bread by their despairing and dirt-poor parents.

story_updates.headline: Humanitarian aid warehouses come under attack in Ukraine
story_updates.summary: Russia’s ongoing full-scale invasion of Ukraine has left civilians vulnerable to repeated deadly attacks and humanitarian workers and key facilities being targeted and destroyed.

story_updates.headline: UN calls for urgent action to protect children from online information risks
story_updates.summary: More than eight in 10 young people aged 15 to 24 worldwide are now online, and in low-income countries they outpace the rest of the population nearly two to one.

story_updates.headline: Afghanistan: UN tells Taliban to open up on abuses committed by security forces
story_updates.summary: Five years into Taliban rule, Afghans still have almost no way of knowing whether soldiers, police and morality officers who abuse their power ever face consequences – and that secrecy is corroding trust in the State, the UN said Monday.

story_updates.headline: DR Congo: Ebola is killing people before they ever reach a doctor
story_updates.summary: More than 1,900 people have died in the Democratic Republic of the Congo's Ebola outbreak – and most of them never made it to a treatment centre. Between 60 and 70 per cent of deaths are happening in communities far from care, a gap that is now central to the World Health Organization's response.

story_updates.headline: UN offers support to Colombia after magnitude 7.4 earthquake kills dozens
story_updates.summary: The UN offered its support to Colombia on Monday after a magnitude 7.4 earthquake struck the west of the country, killing at least 111 people and injuring at least 87, including several children, while leaving others trapped under the rubble and causing landslides and serious damage to homes and infrastructure.

story_updates.headline: Lebanon: UN peacekeepers count hundreds of Israeli strikes and incursions in a single weekend
story_updates.summary: Israeli forces fired 455 projectiles into south Lebanon and breached Lebanese airspace 97 times between Friday and Sunday, the UN's peacekeeping mission in the country reported Monday – among the heaviest fire seen in months.

story_updates.headline: Fighting deepens needs and fuels further displacement in Sudan
story_updates.summary: Ongoing conflict, displacement and funding shortages continue to deepen needs in Sudan, the UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) warned on Monday, underscoring the need for greater civilian protection.

story_updates.headline: Myanmar: UN investigators document deliberate military attacks on civilians
story_updates.summary: Myanmar's military has carried out a sustained campaign of deliberate attacks on civilians – including airstrikes on homes, schools and camps for displaced people, alongside arbitrary detention, torture and sexual violence – according to Human Rights Council-appointed investigators.

story_updates.headline: Colombia earthquake: UN joins national response
story_updates.summary: As earthquake rescue efforts across western Colombia continued on Tuesday, UN agencies said that they stood ready to help “with everything we've got”, in coordination with national authorities.

story_updates.headline: Security Council LIVE: Spotlight on Israeli settler violence in West Bank
story_updates.summary: The Security Council held an open debate on Tuesday which is expected to address escalating Israeli settler violence in the occupied West Bank as attacks on Palestinians and their property continue. UN News app users can follow here.

story_updates.headline: World marks second warmest July on record
story_updates.summary: As multiple regions contend with unbearable heat, drought, wildfires and other extreme weather, the World Meteorological Organization (WMO) on Tuesday underlined the crucial need for stronger forecasts and early warning systems to protect lives and livelihoods.

story_updates.headline: Ebola deaths top 2,000 as scientists race to develop vaccine
story_updates.summary: Local officials in the DR Congo (DRC) reported on Tuesday that deaths from the Ebola virus disease have surpassed 2,000, with half of that number in the last 20 days.

story_updates.headline: South Sudan: UN mission decries deadly attacks, works to calm tensions after ‘nothing but devastation’
story_updates.summary: The UN Mission in South Sudan (UNMISS) has condemned recent armed group attacks in Warrap state which reportedly left more than 60 civilians dead and 50 others injured.

story_updates.headline: After post-pandemic improvement, youth unemployment is rising again
story_updates.summary: Frustrated by skyrocketing youth unemployment, among other issues, tens of thousands of Gen Z activists took to the streets of Nepal last year, demanding a stake in the country’s economic growth. The protest worked and the prime minister resigned.

story_updates.headline: Deadly attack on Red Sea ship adds to global supply chain uncertainty
story_updates.summary: A strike on a merchant ship off the southern coast of Yemen that reportedly killed several seafarers on Tuesday threatens to reignite deep concerns about global trade, amid the ongoing Iran-US war that has choked shipping in the Strait of Hormuz.

story_updates.headline: Five years after Taliban takeover, Afghan women ‘erased from public life’
story_updates.summary: Five years after the Taliban seized power, women and girls in Afghanistan have been systematically stripped of their rights, UN agencies said on Wednesday. De facto authorities have issued more than 100 decrees curbing education, work and freedom of movement – restrictions now compounded by deep cuts to aid on the ground.

story_updates.headline: WHO chief voices concern over Trump Administration’s executive order on vaccines
story_updates.summary: The head of the World Health Organization (WHO) on Wednesday upheld the safety of childhood vaccines in response to a new directive from the White House to overhaul the recommended inoculation schedule.

story_updates.headline: Cholera spreads across borders in West and Central Africa
story_updates.summary: Cholera is spreading rapidly across West and Central Africa, with active outbreaks now in six countries and millions of children at growing risk, UN children’s agency UNICEF has said.

story_updates.headline: Sudan: Attacks and further displacement in Blue Nile and North Kordofan
story_updates.summary: The United Nations has once again urged warring parties in Sudan to protect civilians as the fighting continues to take a heavy toll on the population.

story_updates.headline: Migrant deaths climb sharply in 2026, new UN data shows
story_updates.summary: Severe weather, war, economic pressure and shifting policies reshaped migration journeys across multiple regions in the first four months of 2026, driving a surge in deaths, according to new data released on Wednesday by the International Organization for Migration (IOM).

story_updates.headline: UN continues scaling up response to earthquake in Colombia
story_updates.summary: The UN on Wednesday continued scaling up assistance to areas affected by the deadly earthquake that hit Colombia two days earlier.

story_updates.headline: Youth advocates gather in New York to launch new AI standards
story_updates.summary: As artificial intelligence (AI) rapidly transforms everything from how we learn, to the job market, children are adopting the technology more than three times faster than adults – exposing them to unique opportunities and risks.

story_updates.headline: Occupied West Bank: Settler siege of Palestinians marks a new low: OHCHR
story_updates.summary: In the occupied West Bank, the UN human rights office, OHCHR, appealed on Thursday to Israeli authorities to help Palestinian families trapped in their homes by settlers for days, amid an intensifying campaign to seize their land.

story_updates.headline: Security Council LIVE: Escalating attacks threaten peace in Yemen
story_updates.summary: As tensions triggered by the US-Iran war continue to ripple across the Middle East, the Security Council held an open debate Thursday on Yemen, where escalating deadly military clashes are worsening an already fragile humanitarian situation amid fears that recent Houthi missile strikes on Saudi Arabia and commercial vessels could threaten the 2022 truce between Houthi militia and the internatio...

story_updates.headline: Türkiye’s changes to child detention ‘raise serious human rights concerns’
story_updates.summary: UN human rights chief Volker Türk on Thursday condemned an amendment adopted by Türkiye’s parliament that would allow judges to give life sentences to child offenders convicted of serious crimes.

story_updates.headline: Ukraine: Civilian casualties hit highest level since March 2022
story_updates.summary: Civilian casualties in Ukraine reached their highest monthly level in July, with more people killed and injured than at any time since March 2022, the UN Human Rights Monitoring Mission in the country, HRMMU, said in an update on Thursday.

story_updates.headline: World News in Brief: Afghanistan education, Myanmar flooding, Syria recovery, homecare workers in New York
story_updates.summary: Five years since the Taliban seized power in Kabul, life for some Afghans has improved while many others suffer growing hardship.

story_updates.headline: Ebola tracing improves in DR Congo – but the virus is still winning the race
story_updates.summary: Health authorities in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) are tracking a growing share of people exposed to Ebola, but the epidemic in the country's restive east continues to outpace their ability to find and isolate the sick, the World Health Organization (WHO) has warned.

story_updates.headline: Gaza: Destruction of buildings rises by nearly 10 per cent since ceasefire
story_updates.summary: New satellite assessments show the destruction of buildings in Gaza has climbed by nearly 10 per cent since October’s faltering ceasefire between Hamas and Israeli forces aim to end the two-year war, which reduced cities to rubble and displaced more than one million people, UN agencies said on Thursday.

story_updates.headline: Colombia quake: In Cali’s ruins, an ‘overwhelming sense of humanity’
story_updates.summary: In one of the cities hardest hit by the earthquake that struck Colombia, hundreds of people are still waiting for news of missing relatives, friends and neighbours.

story_updates.headline: Sudan: The harrowing reality of giving birth in a war zone
story_updates.summary: Sudanese women about to give birth are losing their babies and sometimes their own lives because of a lack of specialist healthcare support, amid the ongoing war, UN humanitarians said on Friday.

story_updates.headline: Meth trafficking across Middle East becoming more advanced, UNODC warns
story_updates.summary: Authorities in Iran intercepted 3,663 kilogrammes of methamphetamines headed for Europe and the Persian Gulf in the first quarter of 2026, according to the UN’s drugs and crime fighting agency (UNODC).

story_updates.headline: An attack on healthcare every six hours, and no one held to account
story_updates.summary: Across the world, healthcare has suffered more than 10,000 attacks in the past eight years, including during the brutal conflict in Ukraine and efforts to contain the current Ebola outbreak spreading rapidly in the eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC).

story_updates.headline: 900 obstacles and counting: West Bank families trapped as aid access shrinks
story_updates.summary: Humanitarians continue to provide life-saving assistance to people across the Occupied Palestinian Territory despite facing obstacles such as checkpoints, instability and access restrictions, the United Nations said on Friday.

story_updates.headline: ‘Ebola is winning’: Epidemic now killing one person every 30 minutes
story_updates.summary: The Ebola outbreak in the eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) – the fastest-growing on record and on track to become the deadliest – is killing one person every 30 minutes.

story_updates.headline: ‘Warned but not protected’: Four in ten adults in England ignore heat alerts
story_updates.summary: As amber heat-health alerts spread across England this summer, a new study has found that the warnings are being received – but not changing behaviour.

story_updates.headline: The grass beneath our feet: Why rangelands matter
story_updates.summary: In northern Kenya, a herder scans the sky for rain that hasn't come. The grass his animals need is thinning by the day.

story_updates.headline: Former rebel fighters join campaign against Ebola in the DR Congo
story_updates.summary: Demobilised former combatants are actively joining the fight against Ebola by participating in public information campaigns in the east of the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC).

story_updates.headline: First Person: Syrians lead efforts to clear rubble and rebuild lives
story_updates.summary: Communities in Syria are clearing rubble and rebuilding neighbourhoods and livelihoods torn down in the more than a decade of conflict and crisis in the country.

story_updates.headline: Yemen: Türk alarmed by rising civilian toll, urges restraint
story_updates.summary: Escalating conflict in Yemen is killing and injuring a growing number of civilians, the UN human rights chief warned on Monday, as Houthi rebels also strike Saudi Arabia and Red Sea shipping linked to the wider Iran–US confrontation.

story_updates.headline: Aid workers under fire as drones reshape warfare
story_updates.summary: The UN is warning that aid workers face a deadly and evolving threat, with armed drones reshaping battlefields worldwide – putting humanitarian teams increasingly in the line of fire.

story_updates.headline: Sudan war: 200,000 newly displaced as fighting and floods intensify
story_updates.summary: Intensifying fighting in Sudan has displaced at least another 200,000 people since late 2025, while destructive seasonal floods are compounding the massive humanitarian emergency there, the UN International Organization for Migration (IOM) said on Wednesday.

story_updates.headline: International Criminal Court: New US sanctions ‘a flagrant attack’ against its independence
story_updates.summary: The International Criminal Court (ICC) on Wednesday responded to a new round of US sanctions targeting its president and a senior prosecutor, calling them “a flagrant attack” against the court.

story_updates.headline: Zambia: Arrests and detention of political opponents following election raises concern
story_updates.summary: In the wake of President Hakainde Hichilema of Zambia’s re-election for a second five-year term, UN human rights chief has raised concerns over the reported arrests and detention of political opponents in the country.

story_updates.headline: Raising alarm over new illegal Israeli outposts, UN condemns attacks, incitement against Palestinians
story_updates.summary: Reports of new illegal Israeli outposts in the occupied West Bank raised alarms at UN Headquarters on Wednesday while the UN rights office called on Israel to condemn its national security minister’s words that incite “violence amounting to atrocity crimes” against Palestinians.

story_updates.headline: The clean energy transition needs land. Can it help restore it too?
story_updates.summary: What if the infrastructure needed to fight climate change could also help repair the land beneath it?

story_updates.headline: As elections near, South Sudan risks new atrocity crimes, warns rights probe
story_updates.summary: The under-reported humanitarian crisis in South Sudan risks deepening with the real possibility of further atrocity crimes unless renewed fighting stops, a UN-backed probe said on Thursday.

story_updates.headline: DR Congo receives 70,000 Ebola vaccine doses as Bundibugyo outbreak spreads
story_updates.summary: The Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) will receive 70,000 doses of the Ervebo vaccine from the UN’s international vaccine coordination group (ICG) to protect frontline communities against the Ebola virus disease.

story_updates.headline: Mpox: Children account for half of suspected cases in Guinea-Bissau
story_updates.summary: Children, who are particularly vulnerable to the disease, account for half of the 46 suspected mpox cases identified in Guinea-Bissau – with 16 of them under the age of four.

story_updates.headline: Colombia earthquake: 1.2 million need aid as some communities remain out of reach
story_updates.summary: Ten days after a powerful earthquake struck western Colombia, an estimated 1.2 million people need humanitarian assistance, while some communities have still received little or no aid, UN agencies said on Thursday.

story_updates.headline: Middle East: 94 per cent need shelter in Gaza, Israel ramps up demolitions in Lebanon
story_updates.summary: Ninety-four cent of Gaza’s 2.1 million residents need shelter as Israeli gunfire and strikes continue inside the enclave, UN agencies and peacekeepers warned on Thursday.

story_updates.headline: Russian missiles kill 17 more in Ukraine as Guterres calls for ceasefire
story_updates.summary: Russian ballistic missile strikes killed 17 people and injured more than 40 in and around the Ukrainian capital Kyiv on Thursday, local authorities reported.

story_updates.headline: DR Congo Ebola outbreak spreading exponentially, UN responders warn
story_updates.summary: As the deadliest Ebola outbreak in DR Congo’s history continued spreading on Friday, UN responders renewed their urgent appeal for immediate international support, with existing funding for lifesaving work critically low.

story_updates.headline: Somalia: Humanitarian aid cuts leave millions of children vulnerable to hunger
story_updates.summary: The global funding crisis for humanitarian work is taking a growing toll on the most vulnerable children in Somalia, where some aid programmes and facilities have been forced to shut down.

story_updates.headline: Breaking the silence over sexual violence against men and boys in war
story_updates.summary: Conflicts can expose civilians and detainees to grave abuses; the challenge is not only to document these crimes, but also to ensure all survivors are recognised, protected and able to access justice and care.

story_updates.headline: Sudan war: $22 million education boost to help 200,000 children
story_updates.summary: For millions of children in Sudan, the classroom remains out of reach as the country’s civil war continues to disrupt their education. To help tackle this huge problem, the UN global education fund on Monday announced a $22 million initiative to help 200,000 youngsters return to learning.

story_updates.headline: Security Council LIVE: War, hunger, flooding escalates in Sudan
story_updates.summary: The Security Council is currently hearing top UN officials brief on the latest updates about war-torn Sudan as escalating conflict, drone strikes against civilians, displacement, hunger and flooding affects millions and UN agencies strive to deliver lifesaving aid. UN News app users can follow our live coverage here.

story_updates.headline: Global food supply has become ‘collateral damage’ in conflicts: Secretary-General
story_updates.summary: The disruption of maritime traffic in the Strait of Hormuz, Black Sea and Bab al-Mandab Strait has worsened hunger crises and must immediately end, UN Secretary-General António Guterres said.

story_updates.headline: Security Council LIVE: Civilian suffering grows in Russia-Ukraine war
story_updates.summary: As spiralling drone and missile attacks on civilians in the ongoing Russia-Ukraine war continue, top UN officials told the Security Council on Monday that every diplomatic effort must work towards a full, immediate and unconditional ceasefire. UN News app users can follow our live coverage here.

story_updates.headline: Two UN peacekeepers killed in South Sudan ambush
story_updates.summary: Two UN peacekeepers have been killed and a total of seven people injured after unidentified gunmen ambushed a patrol in South Sudan’s eastern Jonglei state on Monday.

story_updates.headline: Gaza: Children still at risk despite drop in acute hunger
story_updates.summary: Among tent cities pitched on the rubble of destroyed homes in Gaza, children are, by one measure, finally getting enough to eat. By another, however, many of them may never fully recover, according to a new study by the UN Children’s Fund (UNICEF) released on Monday.

story_updates.headline: Can restoring land create jobs? These young entrepreneurs are proving it
story_updates.summary: From Ecuador to Bangladesh, a new generation of entrepreneurs is turning land restoration into economic opportunity. Whether repurposing agricultural waste, building greenhouses or deploying AI-powered sensors, they are showing, with support from a United Nations-backed initiative, that restoring land can also generate income and improve livelihoods.

story_updates.headline: 100 days of Ebola and the race to stop the spread
story_updates.summary: A hundred days after the Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak was declared, the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) is facing an epidemic of an unprecedented scale and efforts must grow to contain the spread in the eastern region and across borders, UN agencies warned on Monday.

story_updates.headline: UN chief, Red Cross renew call for rules on lethal autonomous weapons
story_updates.summary: Amid unconfirmed reports that fully autonomous and AI-guided drones are now being used on the battlefield, UN chief António Guterres and the President of the Red Cross on Tuesday renewed their urgent call for stricter global controls, before it is too late.

story_updates.headline: Japan’s ‘2050 Weather Forecast’ highlights extreme heat in the future
story_updates.summary: As extreme heat becomes an increasingly visible reality across Japan, meteorologists, scientists, businesses and professional footballers are joining forces to encourage stronger climate action and raise awareness of the risks posed by global warming.

story_updates.headline: Land degradation is costing far more than restoring: UN deputy chief
story_updates.summary: Countries are spending too little to restore degraded land even as the economic cost of doing nothing climbs towards $1 trillion a year, UN Deputy Secretary-General Amina Mohammed warned at a major UN land conference in Mongolia.

story_updates.headline: Rohingyas in Myanmar suffering ‘heartbreaking’ misery and cruelty
story_updates.summary: Members of the minority ethnic Rohingya Muslim group in Myanmar are “suffering, misery, and cruelty on multiple levels and across the country that is heartbreaking,” according to the UN High Commissioner for Human Rights.

story_updates.headline: As wars spread, the global food system unravels
story_updates.summary: A family with four children abandoned its farm in Somalia after armed groups arrived and demanded payments for the right to continue cultivating the land. They walked roughly 100 kilometers to a displacement camp. One of the children died along the way.

story_updates.headline: One million children in Afghanistan face deadly malnutrition
story_updates.summary: Some 3.7 million children in Afghanistan are suffering from wasting, one of the most dangerous forms of malnutrition, with around one million currently battling the most severe, life-threatening form of the condition.

story_updates.headline: Haiti ramps up the fight against gangs in the capital, but violence spreads elsewhere
story_updates.summary: The killings in Kenscoff began late Sunday, when armed men descended on the farming community in the hills overlooking Haiti’s capital, setting homes ablaze and attacking residents. By Monday, bodies lay in the streets and survivors were searching for missing relatives.

story_updates.headline: Security Council LIVE: Rising tensions in Gaza, West Bank
story_updates.summary: Amid illegal Israeli settlement surges, continued attacks in Gaza and the West Bank alongside tensions throughout Occupied Palestinian Territory, the Security Council is meeting at 10am (local time) on Wednesday to hear briefings on the latest developments. UN News app users can follow here.

story_updates.headline: Shock and devastation remain, a day after Himalayan flood disaster
story_updates.summary: Amid reports that hundreds of people are still missing in Nepal and China after a floodwater surge slammed into towns and villages on Wednesday, aid teams have been working to reach communities cut off by the disaster.

story_updates.headline: Security Council LIVE: Tracking Syria’s transition
story_updates.summary: As Damascus continues to rebuild after more than a decade of war – from the recent dissolution of the Kurdish-led Syrian Democratic Forces to the United States’ removal of Syria from its sponsors of terrorism list – a top UN official warned the Security Council on Thursday that international support can help tackle outstanding challenges. UN News app users can follow here.

story_updates.headline: Lebanon: Civilian risks grow as military activity continues, UN says
story_updates.summary: Damaged roads, disrupted services and ongoing military activity continue to put civilians at risk in south Lebanon as strikes between Israeli forces and Hezbollah continue, according to the UN’s peacekeeping mission in the country (UNIFIL).

story_updates.headline: UN chief condemns ‘indifference’ as Ebola cases mount in DR Congo
story_updates.summary: The Ebola Bundibugyo outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) requires “urgent” action and funding to rein in its alarming spread, the UN Secretary-General told reporters at UN Headquarters on Thursday.

story_updates.headline: After Israeli seizure of Kalandia training centre, UNRWA warns of impact on youth
story_updates.summary: The seizure of a vocational training centre in occupied East Jerusalem has left hundreds of Palestinian young people without access to skills and training that could help shape their futures.

story_updates.headline: Aid reaches hundreds of thousands in Gaza amid severe food insecurity
story_updates.summary: As hunger deepens across Gaza, humanitarian agencies continue to deliver food and other essential supplies to families in need.

story_updates.headline: ‘Immense impact’ of Nepal flood disaster highlighted as casualties mount
story_updates.summary: The impact of the deadly flood in Nepal has been described as “immense” as the authorities there confirm that 538 bodies have been recovered from the disaster-stricken area.

story_updates.headline: Security Council LIVE: Deadly gang attacks spike in Haiti
story_updates.summary: Following a deadly spate of gang attacks on civilians in Haiti and amid reports of illicit weapons slipping into the Caribbean country, the Security Council has called an emergency meeting at 3pm (local time) to hear and discuss the latest developments. UN News app users can follow our coverage here.

story_updates.headline: Risks of child recruitment by armed groups rise in post-quake Colombia
story_updates.summary: The recent earthquake in Colombia could increase the risk of child recruitment by armed groups in Chocó and Valle del Cauca, where thousands of children remain out of school in areas already affected by conflict, the UN warned on Friday.

story_updates.headline: WHO reports more than 3,200 attacks on Ukraine’s healthcare system since full-scale invasion
story_updates.summary: Since the beginning of Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine, 3,205 attacks on healthcare facilities have been carried out, World Health Organization (WHO) Representative for Ukraine Jarno Habicht reported on Friday following fresh overnight strikes.

story_updates.headline: As the Himalayas melt, deadly floods become the new normal
story_updates.summary: A day before a wall of ice, rock and muddy water tore through Himalayan valleys along the Nepal-China border, Dipesh Chapagain was discussing with a colleague just how devastating such a disaster could be.

story_updates.headline: Four children killed as separate attacks in Gaza destroy aid supplies
story_updates.summary: Israeli attacks killed four children and destroyed humanitarian aid supplies in what turned out to be a deadly week in war-ravaged Gaza, the UN emergency relief agency, OCHA, said on Friday.

story_updates.headline: Rising seas, rising stakes: What increasing sea-levels mean to humanity
story_updates.summary: The ocean is rising faster now than at any point in recorded history. The impacts are already being felt and the threats are growing.

story_updates.headline: ‘The lake is our life’: Protecting a shared lifeline in Uganda
story_updates.summary: On the shores of Nkondo, in Uganda’s Kikuube district, the day begins before sunrise. Fishers enter the lake to fish, while families around Lake Albert rely on its waters for food, income and daily survival.

story_updates.headline: Repeated attacks on humanitarian warehouses put vital medical aid at risk in Ukraine: WHO
story_updates.summary: A new airstrike overnight damaged one of the main warehouses used by the World Health Organization (WHO) in Ukraine to store humanitarian medical supplies in the Kyiv region, the UN agency said on Friday.

story_updates.headline: UN aims to raise nearly $50 million for Nepal flood response
story_updates.summary: The UN and its humanitarian partners launched a $49.6 million flash appeal on Friday to deliver emergency assistance to more than 84,000 people affected by last week’s catastrophic floods in Nepal.

story_updates.headline: West Bank: UN rights report warns of forcible displacement from three refugee camps
story_updates.summary: Israeli security forces forcibly displaced the entire population of three Palestine refugee camps in the occupied West Bank in January and February last year – and continue to prevent their return, in violation of international law, according to a new report by the UN human rights office, OHCHR.

story_updates.headline: UN tells the world: Stop making Africa look small
story_updates.summary: The UN General Assembly has voted overwhelmingly to encourage governments, schools and tech companies worldwide to stop using maps that make Africa look far smaller than it really is.

story_updates.headline: As wildfires spread north, UN agencies race to help Europe adapt
story_updates.summary: As the climate warms, the threat of wildfires is spreading in Europe. How can historically cooler and wetter countries prepare?

story_updates.headline: Central Park adapts to climate change while helping New York stay cool
story_updates.summary: In the heart of Manhattan in New York City, the effects of climate change are becoming increasingly visible.

story_updates.headline: New reservoir offers innovative solution to South Sudan cattle beef
story_updates.summary: At the end of a history-laden path winding through palm trees and scattered ruins – remnants of once-vibrant villages destroyed by cattle raids – lies a rare sight in this dry part of Terekeka county in South Sudan: a sparkling, fresh water source.

story_updates.headline: ‘Advance safety for all’: International police cooperation helps tackle cross-border crime
story_updates.summary: As criminal networks increasingly exploit weak institutions and operate across borders, the UN says no police force can tackle them alone.

story_updates.headline: Coordinated action on clean air and climate change can net $15 for every dollar spent
story_updates.summary: Tackling air pollution and climate change together can save millions of lives, reduce global warming and generate roughly $15 in economic benefits for every $1 spent, a new UN-backed report has revealed.

story_updates.headline: Human rights chief Türk renews call for end to spiralling Sudan war
story_updates.summary: The ongoing war in Sudan took centre stage at the UN Human Rights Council on Monday where the UN High Commissioner for Human Rights, Volker Türk, led calls for an end to attacks on civilians in “markets, hospitals [and] fuel stations”.

story_updates.headline: AI: Türk urges action before it becomes an ‘existential risk to humanity’
story_updates.summary: UN human rights chief Volker Türk added his voice on Monday to growing calls for greater AI controls, warning that the revolutionary technology could become an “existential risk to humanity” if left unchecked.

story_updates.headline: Terrorist propaganda is outpacing global efforts to stop it, UN report finds
story_updates.summary: Terrorist groups are recruiting, raising money and even planning operations through propaganda that is now “embedded” in every stage of their work, a new UN report warns – and governments are struggling to keep pace.

story_updates.headline: Surge in displacement following fighting in southwest Yemen
story_updates.summary: At least 46,000 people have been displaced since renewed fighting last week between Houthi rebels and pro-government forces in southwestern Yemen, the International Organization for Migration (IOM) reported on Friday.

story_updates.headline: The world just had the hottest August ever
story_updates.summary: Earth just had the hottest August on record, according to newly released weather data.

story_updates.headline: Security Council LIVE: Ambassadors mark 9/11 with counter-terrorism push on AI and drones
story_updates.summary: The Security Council met to mark 25 years since the 9/11 attacks with a briefing on counter-terrorism as ambassadors take stock of a threat that has morphed dramatically since resolution 1373 built the council's counter-terrorism machinery in 2001. Briefers highlighted militants' growing use of artificial intelligence, drones and encrypted platforms for recruitment and attack planning.

story_updates.headline: ‘Where do we go?’: How Israel’s ‘yellow line’ is closing in on Palestinians
story_updates.summary: Ola Ishtiwi sits with her children in front of the remains of her home in the Al-Tuffah neighbourhood in eastern Gaza City, a few metres away from a series of painted cement blocks Israel has placed to mark what has become known as the “yellow line”.

story_updates.headline: Married at 13, pregnant and starving: Child brides of Yemen
story_updates.summary: Fatimah* was 13 when she was married off to an older man. Two years later, she gave birth to twin daughters.

story_updates.headline: Guterres: Old global order must change as power shifts to emerging economies
story_updates.summary: UN Secretary-General António Guterres told leaders of a bloc of major emerging economies in New Delhi on Sunday that a more balanced global order requires an overhaul of the institutions built after the Second World War, including the UN Security Council.

story_updates.headline: South Sudan: UNICEF reaches communities cut off by conflict in Jonglei state
story_updates.summary: The UN Children’s Fund (UNICEF) and partners have delivered lifesaving assistance to families in conflict-affected communities in South Sudan’s Jonglei state, many of whom had gone months without humanitarian support.

story_updates.headline: World fears major war more than any other global risk, UN survey finds
story_updates.summary: Two years ago, the idea of a large-scale war breaking out felt like a distant hypothetical to the experts who help chart the world’s dangers. Today it tops their list of fears, according to a new UN Global Risk Report.

story_updates.headline: ‘Super El Niño’ deepens hunger crisis in South Sudan – WFP
story_updates.summary: The already dire hunger crisis in South Sudan is becoming increasingly critical as violence, extreme weather and dwindling aid leave millions without enough food, the UN World Food Programme (WFP) warned on Tuesday.

story_updates.headline: Gaza remains recovery points to possible war crimes, says UN rights chief
story_updates.summary: Bodies are still being pulled from the rubble of Gaza, three years after Israeli bombardment flattened entire neighbourhoods – most of them women and children.

story_updates.headline: Ukraine: Attacks on education threaten an entire generation, UNICEF warns
story_updates.summary: In an underground classroom in Sumy, Ukraine, children sit quietly at their desks, busy with the day’s lessons. For the moment they are shielded from the horrors of nearly five years of war, but just barely.

story_updates.headline: Back to school in Haiti: ‘Madame, can you stop what the gangs are doing to us?’
story_updates.summary: When UNICEF’s Representative in Haiti Geetanjali Narayan stepped into a classroom in Port-au-Prince at the start of the new school year, she asked the children a simple question: What did they most need from the UN children’s agency?

story_updates.headline: Ebola responders grapple with widening outbreak in DR Congo
story_updates.summary: The deadly Ebola virus outbreak in DR Congo continues to spread across the vast country despite some success in containing it, aid officials said on Tuesday, in a renewed call for international support to help responders on the ground.

story_updates.headline: Escalating conflict drives new displacement in Yemen
story_updates.summary: The escalating conflict in Yemen is choking off aid shipments and driving fresh displacement, including to nearby Djibouti, with UN agencies reporting on Tuesday that nearly 100,000 people have been displaced since fighting intensified earlier this month.

story_updates.headline: UNICEF says thousands of children require mental health support after Nepal floods
story_updates.summary: Three weeks after the devastating flash floods in Nepal, about 17,000 children require urgent mental health and psychosocial support in the country, the UN Children’s Fund (UNICEF) said on Tuesday.
