story_updates.headline: Security Council LIVE: Rising violence triggers emergency meeting on Yemen
story_updates.summary: Amid rising violence in Yemen, the Security Council met in emergency session on Tuesday to discuss the situation surrounding the critical Bab el-Mandeb Strait shipping route as UN agencies warn of rising displacement, including thousands of Yemenis fleeing to Djibouti. UN News app users can follow here.

story_updates.headline: UN report warns of reprisals against those who collaborate in defence of human rights
story_updates.summary: Activists, lawyers and others who cooperate with the United Nations on human rights continue to face intimidation and reprisals, according to a new report issued on Wednesday by the Secretary-General that calls for greater protection and accountability.

story_updates.headline: Gaza: At least 20 killed in deadly building collapse, search for survivors continues
story_updates.summary: Search and rescue operations continued in Gaza City on Wednesday following the collapse of a bombed-out building that killed at least 20 people, according to reports.

story_updates.headline: Security Council LIVE: ‘Being a woman is a crime in Afghanistan,’ civil society briefer declares
story_updates.summary: Since the Taliban returned to power in Afghanistan in 2021, the continuing presence of terrorist groups as well as rights violations against women and girls are a growing concern as the Security Council met Wednesday to hear latest developments, including from a civil society representative who said being born as a woman in the country “is a crime”. Follow full coverage here.

story_updates.headline: Repression continues in Venezuela in the face of ‘appalling’ human rights violations
story_updates.summary: In Venezuela’s El Rodeo maximum security prison, some of those detained for political reasons are subject to forced intubation – and prolonged confinement in a sealed underground cistern.

story_updates.headline: World News in Brief: Shipping alert from IMO, democracy vanishing in Nicaragua, alert over political ‘denialism’
story_updates.summary: Amid a rising number of attacks on shipping in key waterways in the Middle East linked to the US-Iran war, the head of UN maritime agency, Mr. Arsenio Dominguez, has insisted that the conflict is not a “pretext” to target “innocent seafarers”.

story_updates.headline: Who should set the rules for AI? The UN is pushing for a safer digital future
story_updates.summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) is advancing rapidly, raising questions about how societies and governments can capture its benefits while managing risks that often extend beyond national borders.

story_updates.headline: The world comes to New York: What’s at stake at UN General Assembly high-level week
story_updates.summary: Each September, New York becomes the centre of global diplomacy as presidents, prime ministers, ministers and diplomats from around the world gather at United Nations Headquarters.

story_updates.headline: AI, climate and conflicts top Guterres’s agenda ahead of General Assembly
story_updates.summary: Ahead of the UN General Assembly’s high-level week, Secretary-General António Guterres said the world had entered “an era of deep uncertainty” and urged governments to embrace international cooperation to address global threats.

story_updates.headline: As freshwater reserves shrink, countries must prepare for a new water reality
story_updates.summary: The world is entering a period in which abnormal water supplies are becoming the norm, with river flows, groundwater and glaciers all showing signs of sustained disruption, the UN weather agency warned on Thursday.

story_updates.headline: Yemen escalation displaces more than 57,000 children: UNICEF
story_updates.summary: Renewed fighting in Yemen is deepening an already severe humanitarian crisis in a country where more than 12 million children depend on aid, after more than a decade of conflict.

story_updates.headline: Security Council LIVE: Syria’s transition in the spotlight
story_updates.summary: While Syria is making progress in its political transition, the Security Council is meeting to hear briefings and discuss the situation on the ground, including recent reports of deadly armed clashes with an ISIS-affiliate terrorist group in the south and protests over rising fuel prices.

story_updates.headline: Guterres calls for action as hate speech spreads across new platforms online
story_updates.summary: The UN Secretary-General has called for concerted action by governments, technology companies and civil society to stamp out hate speech, emphasizing that “its toxic message is spreading fast and striking deep”.

story_updates.headline: UN fact-finding mission on Iran focuses on plight of civilians
story_updates.summary: The Independent International Fact-Finding Mission on Iran confirmed that civilians in the country suffered serious human rights violations and “crimes against humanity committed by their government,” while finding "reasonable grounds" to believe that the United States committed “war crimes” in the context of its ongoing conflict with the Islamic Republic.

story_updates.headline: Gender equality woefully off track, new UN report reveals
story_updates.summary: At the current rate of progress, gender equality would take 171 years to achieve, a new UN report finds as institutions built to advance gains are being defunded and demobilised.

story_updates.headline: World News in Brief: Winter aid for Gaza, West Bank; Haiti food production; migrant deaths at sea; human rights funding
story_updates.summary: The UN Children’s Fund (UNICEF) is seeking to raise $97.5 million to protect 540,000 children and their families in Gaza and the West Bank from harsh winter conditions in the coming months.

story_updates.headline: New UN system platform puts millions of data points at users’ fingertips, says Guterres
story_updates.summary: How do you make sense of a world facing interconnected crises, from poverty and hunger to climate change, if the facts are scattered across dozens of different places?

story_updates.headline: The race to build a pandemic-proof world
story_updates.summary: Six years after COVID-19 killed millions, battered health systems, disrupted lives and brought the global economy to a virtual standstill, the world is still grappling with how we can prepare better for the next pandemic.

story_updates.headline: Why the UN General Assembly still matters
story_updates.summary: More than eight decades on from its founding, the UN General Assembly remains the place where the UN’s 193 Member States come together to debate the defining challenges of the day, from war and peace – to development, climate change and human rights.

story_updates.headline: The right to development: Why equity, not charity, is a human right
story_updates.summary: Compare two children born in the same year: one in a country with functioning schools, social services, fair elections and a dynamic economy and the other in a nation devastated by poverty, conflict, climate change or corruption.

story_updates.headline: Displacement on the rise in Yemen as fighting continues
story_updates.summary: As hostilities worsen in Yemen, more people have been fleeing their homes, further intensifying the humanitarian crisis within the region, the UN Refugee Agency (UNHCR) warned on Tuesday.

story_updates.headline: Guterres: ‘Cracks have become canyons’ as world faces four tests of power
story_updates.summary: Humanity faces four defining “tests of power” – around war or peace, inequality, climate change and AI – that will determine whether the world moves towards a new era of cooperation or deeper division, the UN chief warned the General Assembly on Tuesday.

story_updates.headline: Millions of children return to schools that still can’t provide clean water or a working toilet
story_updates.summary: A new academic year is underway in many countries across the world, yet millions of children still attend schools where the water is unsafe to drink, toilets are unusable and there is nowhere to properly wash their hands.

story_updates.headline: When a country goes underwater: Island States fight for their future
story_updates.summary: Rising sea levels and ever-more-powerful storms are eroding shorelines, submerging land and threatening to evict millions of people from their homes worldwide.

story_updates.headline: UN rendered unable to fulfil its mission, Turkish President laments before world leaders
story_updates.summary: The United Nations continues to be weakened, and those who have tied their hopes to the world body – from Palestine to Sudan – have been disappointed, Türkiye’s President said, while adding that his country is committed to restoring confidence in the Organization.

story_updates.headline: Qatar: Absence of a regional collective security system is fuelling crisis in the Gulf
story_updates.summary: The crisis in the Gulf should come as a surprise to no one, the Emir of Qatar, Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani said on Tuesday, describing it as the cumulative result of years of delay, crisis management through temporary fixes, and unrealistic policies.

story_updates.headline: ‘Time is running out’ for Israel-Palestine two-State solution
story_updates.summary: The UN chief warned on Tuesday that the two-State solution for the Israel-Palestine conflict is at risk of collapse amid illegal Israeli settlement expansion and annexation.

story_updates.headline: Choose international order over ‘law of the jungle’, urges Macron
story_updates.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron said on Tuesday that the world faces a stark choice: “Do we want to live…with a return to the law of the jungle – or do we want to live in a civilized international society?”

story_updates.headline: ‘Ask us first’: Children demand a voice on AI’s future
story_updates.summary: The first generation to grow up with AI may also be the last one anyone thinks to ask about it – and that has to change, the UN's top human rights official said on Tuesday.

story_updates.headline: How El Niño offers a test of whether the world can adapt to a changing climate
story_updates.summary: El Niño is strengthening in a world that is already hotter, raising the risk of drought, floods and crop losses across some of the world’s most important food-producing regions. But unlike many disasters, this one can be seen coming. UN experts say the months ahead offer countries a chance not only to protect the next harvest and our food security, but to prepare for a more unpredictable climat...

story_updates.headline: Time to accept ‘hard truths’ so trust can be rebuilt: General Assembly President
story_updates.summary: The UN’s survival for 80 years is not, by itself, proof of success, and now, the institution must confront painful truths if it hopes to rebuild public trust, said Khalilur Rahman, president of the General Assembly’s 81st session on Tuesday.

story_updates.headline: Diplomacy is the way to address global challenges, Brazil tells General Assembly
story_updates.summary: Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva told the General Assembly on Tuesday that the UN needs to become a “temple of peace” once again, as it confronts one of the most critical periods in its 80-year history.

story_updates.headline: Trump defends military action against Iran, Venezuela, and calls for rebrand of AI
story_updates.summary: US President Donald Trump used his address to the UN General Assembly on Tuesday to defend recent military action against Iran, urging countries to maintain economic pressure on Tehran – and declaring that he now faces a choice between making a deal, or taking far more drastic steps.

story_updates.headline: LIVE: Climate change is here - What happens next is still in our hands
story_updates.summary: From deadly floods in the Himalayas to wildfires and extreme heat across Europe, 2026 has brought a succession of stark reminders of a changing climate. The task is immediate: Protect people from the impacts already unfolding while rapidly cutting the emissions of harmful gasses driving climate change. World leaders have been meeting on Wednesday to discuss how to turn those priorities into act...

story_updates.headline: Right to development: A blueprint for unmet promises
story_updates.summary: Ahead of the 40th anniversary of the groundbreaking Declaration on the Right to Development this December, world leaders gathered at a High-Level Week meeting on Wednesday to map progress made and the 21st century challenges still ahead – from narrowing the digital divide to levelling the AI playing field – as the UN chief presented a “blueprint” to address promises that remain unfulfilled.

story_updates.headline: DR Congo Ebola outbreak toll exceeds 3,700 deaths
story_updates.summary: More than 130 days into the latest Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), health experts said on Wednesday that response efforts have been scaled up significantly and “the first encouraging signs of progress” are now being seen.

story_updates.headline: UN health agency calls for investment boost to save young lives from cancer
story_updates.summary: More children and young people are beating cancer, but progress remains uneven across regions and age groups, highlighting the need for increased investment to boost survival rates.

story_updates.headline: Security Council LIVE: World leaders debate ongoing war in Ukraine
story_updates.summary: Five years of war. Another winter closing in. Today, the Security Council once again debates a path to peace – though any resolution still runs up against the veto of Russia, one of its own permanent members, whose objections have repeatedly stalled any consensus. As world leaders take the floor, the gap between diplomatic process and battlefield reality appears to be stark.

story_updates.headline: LIVE: OpenAI and Anthropic brief Security Council amid ‘real and imminent’ threat posed by runaway AI
story_updates.summary: The Security Council has been briefed by some of the world's top AI executives on the huge benefits and huge risks the frontier technology presents. With warnings mounting that the world may be losing its grip on systems built to outthink us, Yoshua Bengio, a recipient of the prestigious Turing Award and one of the godfathers of machine intelligence, said the dangers of AI beyond human control...

story_updates.headline: Zelenskyy urges stronger pressure on Russia, warns war’s impact is spreading beyond Ukraine
story_updates.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy on Wednesday called for intensified pressure on Russia to end its war against Ukraine, arguing that Moscow continues to incur massive losses while prolonging a conflict whose consequences are increasingly being felt far beyond the battlefield.

story_updates.headline: Rohingya refugees deserve a future beyond survival, not endless displacement
story_updates.summary: Nine years after the mass displacement of the Rohingya from Myanmar, their situation remains one of the world's most protracted and complex refugee crises, marked by years of persecution and uncertainty over the prospect of returning home.

story_updates.headline: Guterres calls on countries to set clear timelines for transition away from fossil fuels
story_updates.summary: “We are the first generation with the tools to end the fossil fuel age – and the last who can avert climate catastrophe,” UN Secretary-General António Guterres said on Wednesday, calling on countries to draw up credible roadmaps with clear timelines to transition away from fossil fuels.

story_updates.headline: Venezuela seeking rebirth after political crisis and devastating earthquakes, President tells UN
story_updates.summary: Venezuela is seeking to rebuild after a period of political upheaval and the destruction caused by twin earthquakes earlier this year, Acting President Delcy Rodríguez told world leaders at the United Nations on Wednesday.

story_updates.headline: United Kingdom announces action on disinformation and global AI standards
story_updates.summary: The United Kingdom will fight disinformation at home and abroad, and work to ensure global safety standards for artificial intelligence (AI), new Prime Minister Andy Burnham said on Monday evening in his first address to the United Nations General Assembly.

story_updates.headline: Syria begins ‘new phase of revival’, President Al-Sharaa tells General Assembly
story_updates.summary: Syrian President Ahmad Al-Sharaa told the UN General Assembly on Wednesday that his country “is rising” on many levels, thanks to the strength of its people.

story_updates.headline: At UN, Pezeshkian turns terrorism accusation back on Iran’s critics
story_updates.summary: President Masoud Pezeshkian opened his General Assembly address with a direct rebuttal to US President Donald Trump, who a day earlier had branded Iran the “number one sponsor of terror.”

story_updates.headline: UN’s ‘sacred covenant has been broken’, Argentina’s Milei tells General Assembly
story_updates.summary: Argentine President Javier Milei told the General Assembly on Wednesday that the UN has broken the “sacred covenant” on which it was founded, failing at what it was meant to do – while excelling at things beyond its remit.

story_updates.headline: Equality ‘ends at the doors of the Security Council’, Kenya’s Ruto tells General Assembly
story_updates.summary: Kenyan President William Ruto told the General Assembly on Wednesday that the sovereign equality the UN proclaims is contradicted by its own structures, urging Member States to reform the Security Council and an international financial system “built for another age”.

story_updates.headline: LIVE: World leaders approve new declaration to tackle rising sea levels
story_updates.summary: Sea level rise is among the most visible consequences of global warming, but for some countries, it is an imminent existential threat. World leaders approved a new declaration on Thursday while debating the best ways to strengthen international cooperation and support vulnerable low-lying nations most at risk.

story_updates.headline: World News in Brief: ‘New intensity’ to Russian attacks on Ukraine, Yemen, Gaza and Colombia updates
story_updates.summary: Russian armed forces have carried out repeated attacks across Ukraine over the past several days, killing and injuring civilians and damaging homes, hospitals, shops and workplaces, UN human rights monitors said on Thursday.

story_updates.headline: UNRWA work and mandate in ‘jeopardy’, Guterres warns
story_updates.summary: The UN Relief and Works Agency for Palestine refugees (UNRWA) continues to operate under “extraordinary pressure”, UN Secretary-General António Guterres said on Thursday.

story_updates.headline: Haitians can’t wait to return home and vote in elections says Prime Minister
story_updates.summary: “There is a people. A people who can wait no longer.  A people waiting to regain security, to return home to work, to send their children to school, and to freely choose their leaders.” Those are the words of the Haitian Prime Minister, Alix Didier Fils-Aimé, who spoke at a special UN meeting on the future of security in Haiti.

story_updates.headline: ‘Rising seas are sinking futures’
story_updates.summary: World leaders approved the UN Declaration on Sea Level Rise by consensus on Thursday as the UN chief warned that encroaching waters are already threatening the future of coastal communities worldwide.

story_updates.headline: ‘Turn what we know into what we do,’ Barbados PM Mottley urges world leaders at UN
story_updates.summary: Barbados Prime Minister Mia Mottley called on world leaders on Thursday to turn knowledge into action, reform international institutions and ensure that new technologies and global wealth benefit everyone.

story_updates.headline: The Takeaway: UN General Assembly debate Day 2
story_updates.summary: This edition of UN News's The Takeaway recaps key highlghts at the UN General Assembly on Wednesday, including focus on the war in Ukraine and a renewed push by African countries for Security Council reform.

story_updates.headline: ‘Peace remains only a promise’ for millions in eastern DR Congo, General Assembly hears
story_updates.summary: The Prime Minister of the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) cautioned against growing global demand for “blood-stained minerals” in the rush to net-zero, in her speech to the UN General Assembly.

story_updates.headline: Palestinian existence under threat, Abbas tells UN, warning of ‘another Nakba’
story_updates.summary: Israeli policies now threaten “the very life and existence of the Palestinian people on their homeland”, Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas told the UN General Assembly on Thursday, urging the world not to allow “another Nakba”.

story_updates.headline: Israeli leader at UN: ‘We’re going to win. We have no other choice’
story_updates.summary: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu used his address to the UN General Assembly to defend Israel’s strikes against Iran as a matter of national survival and described the violence in the West Bank as the work of a few “juvenile delinquents” and rejected accusations of genocide in Gaza as “the greatest lie of the century.”

story_updates.headline: Yemen’s path to stability depends on restoring the state, Leadership Council vice-president tells UN
story_updates.summary: The Vice-President of Yemen’s Presidential Leadership Council, Abdullah Al-Alimi Bawazir, told the UN General Assembly on Thursday that his Government had engaged “responsibly and positively” with regional and international peace initiatives and made significant concessions to end the suffering of the Yemeni people.

story_updates.headline: Yemen violence deepens concerns over child hunger crisis
story_updates.summary: Aid agencies in Yemen highlighted the growing hunger emergency sparked by renewed fighting between Houthi opposition forces and Government troops, after mobile health clinics reported that hundreds of children displaced by the violence are suffering from the most deadly form of malnutrition.

story_updates.headline: LIVE: Six years on from COVID-19, is the world ready for the next pandemic?
story_updates.summary: COVID-19 killed millions, shattered health systems and brought the global economy to a virtual standstill. World leaders are meeting Friday to review the lessons learned and cement a new approach to prevention and preparation for the next pandemic. Hopes are high that a World Health Organization-led international agreement can move forward.

story_updates.headline: Security Council LIVE: Rising tide of forced displacement
story_updates.summary: At a time when war, climate crises and man-made disasters continue to displace millions around the world, the UN High Commissioner for Refugees will brief the Security Council on Friday.

story_updates.headline: Sudan’s farmers are ready to return – private investment could get them there
story_updates.summary: The war in Sudan has devastated the economy and agricultural production, but a UN-backed plan aims to mobilise private sector investment to help farmers return to their fields.

story_updates.headline: Africa needs its own AI solutions, not borrowed ones, says expert
story_updates.summary: Africa should focus its use of technology on solving its own real challenges rather than copying the systems and priorities of other parts of the world.

story_updates.headline: ‘Invest with Iraq’: PM sets out vision for new economic future
story_updates.summary: Iraq’s Prime Minister, Ali Faleh Al-Zaidi, said his country aims to exert its influence as an active economic power in the region, and as a bridge for dialogue and cooperation between its peoples.

story_updates.headline: ‘No one speaks on behalf of Lebanon’: PM Salam asserts State authority at UN
story_updates.summary: Lebanon’s Prime Minister, Nawaf Salam, has stressed that decisions over war and peace, and control of weapons, must rest solely with the State and its constitutional institutions.

story_updates.headline: World News in Brief: West Bank demolitions accelerate, urgent support for Sudan, Haiti diplacement, AI hub to boost gender equality
story_updates.summary: The situation in the occupied West Bank continues to deteriorate, the UN human rights office has said, pointing to the “mass destruction” of Palestinian villages and forcible transfer of residents in Msafer Yatta, South Hebron Hills.

story_updates.headline: UN voices grave concern as fighting spreads across northern Ethiopia
story_updates.summary: The UN said on Friday it remains gravely concerned by the continued deterioration of the security situation across northern Ethiopia, as fighting spreads across multiple fronts and increasingly disrupts humanitarian operations.

story_updates.headline: Australia urges global cooperation on climate, AI checks and international law
story_updates.summary: Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese underlined the need for countries to work together to address the climate crisis, emerging technologies such as AI, and the breakdown of international rules, at the United Nations General Assembly on Thursday.

story_updates.headline: Nepal PM urges climate justice after ‘Himalayan tsunami’ devastates country
story_updates.summary: Nepal’s Prime Minister Balendra Shah brought a stark warning from the Himalayas to the UN General Assembly on Thursday, saying catastrophic floods that killed at least 1,400 people in his country laid bare the human cost of climate change, and the failure of the international system to protect those least responsible for it.

story_updates.headline: Tuvalu urges decisive global action as rising seas threaten its future
story_updates.summary: Climate change remains the greatest existential threat to Tuvalu, Prime Minister Feleti Teo told the UN General Assembly on Friday, warning that the pace and scale of international action are still falling far short of what vulnerable island nations need.

story_updates.headline: Pakistan’s Sharif warns any diversion of Indus waters will be ‘treated as an act of war’
story_updates.summary: Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif told the UN General Assembly on Friday that any attempt by India to stop, impede or divert Pakistan’s share of the Indus River waters “will be treated as an act of war”.

story_updates.headline: Haiti at ‘watershed moment’, Prime Minister tells UN, urging full backing for security force
story_updates.summary: Haiti is at a “watershed moment” in its struggle against gang violence and needs sustained international support alongside stronger national security institutions, Prime Minister Alix Didier Fils-Aimé told the UN General Assembly on Friday.

story_updates.headline: Countries adopt global blueprint to tackle fast-evolving crime in digital age
story_updates.summary: Countries adopted on Saturday a new global blueprint for tackling rapidly evolving forms of crime, as the UN’s largest gathering on crime prevention and criminal justice opened in Abu Dhabi with a call for stronger international cooperation.

story_updates.headline: Saudi Arabia warns Gulf security inseparable from global stability amid regional tensions
story_updates.summary: Saudi Arabia’s Foreign Minister warned on Saturday that escalating threats across the Middle East risked international peace, energy security and global trade, calling for stronger international cooperation to protect Gulf States and vital shipping routes.

story_updates.headline: Countries far from conflict paying the price for wars not their own, India tells UN
story_updates.summary: India’s External Affairs Minister Subrahmanyam Jaishankar warned on Saturday that violent conflicts continue to undermine international peace and security, while countries far removed from the battlefield are being forced to pay a heavy price.

story_updates.headline: The Takeaway: UN General Assembly debate Day 4
story_updates.summary: From the Caribbean to the Pacific, leaders from small island States demanded climate justice, ocean protection and greater solidarity at the UN General Assembly on Friday.  They warned that rising seas are already redrawing national boundaries, while the ripple effects of faraway wars are being felt on their shores. This edition of The Takeaway summarizes key points made during the fourth...

story_updates.headline: ‘Safeguard the postwar order,’ China tells UN General Assembly
story_updates.summary: China's Vice President, Han Zheng, urged the world to defend the postwar international order on Saturday, telling the UN General Assembly that geopolitical conflicts, widening development gaps and mounting global challenges make multilateralism more urgent than ever.

story_updates.headline: Lavrov issues call for new Eurasian ‘security architecture’
story_updates.summary: Russia's Foreign Minister, Sergey Lavrov, accused Western countries of destabilising the world through “force and double standards” in his address to the UN General Assembly on Saturday, vowing that Moscow's “special military operation” in Ukraine would be “carried through to the end.”

story_updates.headline: Cuba warns against ‘law of the jungle’ as Foreign Minister denounces US pressure
story_updates.summary: Cuba’s Foreign Minister warned the UN General Assembly on Saturday that escalating military and economic pressure in Latin America and the Caribbean was threatening international law, while accusing the United States of intensifying a decades-long campaign to isolate and weaken his country.

story_updates.headline: Canada urges stronger partnerships as global order faces ‘rupture’
story_updates.summary: Canada’s Foreign Minister Anita Anand warned the UN General Assembly on Saturday that the international order has entered an era of profound disruption, calling for stronger multilateral cooperation and new partnerships as major powers increasingly turn away from global economic integration.

story_updates.headline: Security Council LIVE: Ambassadors meet as West Bank tensions rise, Gaza plan stalls
story_updates.summary: The Security Council met Monday morning with prospects for peace in the Middle East under strain on two fronts. In the West Bank, settler violence and settlement expansion are raising fears for a two-State solution. In Gaza, a year-old peace plan has stalled while civilian suffering continues. The meeting comes as the plan’s remaining phases, including Hamas’ disarmament and Israel’s full withd...

story_updates.headline: DR Congo Ebola emergency: Calls grow for urgent humanitarian access
story_updates.summary: Aid teams trying to keep deadly Ebola disease from spreading in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) are increasingly concerned about ongoing fighting and violence that has forced thousands of people to flee a displacement camp in the vast, resource-rich east of the country.

story_updates.headline: World News in Brief: Refugee funding, US migration policy triggers ‘cascade’ of rights violations, world forests report, restorative…
story_updates.summary: Support for water and sanitation at the biggest camp in the world for Syrian refugees is under threat from a lack of funding – combined with the impact of climate change – the UN Children’s Fund, UNICEF, said on Monday.

story_updates.headline: From energy crisis to energy transition: How renewables are reshaping energy security
story_updates.summary: The continuing conflict in the Middle East is disrupting global energy markets and pushing up fuel prices, with knock-on effects far beyond the region.

story_updates.headline: UN leaders renew push to defeat racism, 25 years after Durban
story_updates.summary: “No country is free of racism.” That warning from US youth activist Marley Dias set the tone on Monday as UN Member States reinvigorated global efforts against racism, discrimination and xenophobia with a new declaration.

story_updates.headline: LIVE: World leaders take stock of global fight against racism
story_updates.summary: World leaders met in the General Assembly Monday to assess how far the world has come in combating racism and how far it still has to go. The Durban Declaration and Programme of Action, the most comprehensive framework of its kind, seeks to acknowledge historical injustices, dismantle inequalities and build societies grounded in dignity, equality and justice for all.

story_updates.headline: Sudan tells UN: No imposed solutions to country’s conflict
story_updates.summary: Sudan’s Foreign Minister addressed the UN General Assembly on Monday in place of Chairperson of the Transitional Sovereignty Council, Abdel Fattah al-Burhan, whose visa application was rejected by Washington.

story_updates.headline: ‘Ballot must replace the bullets’, South Sudan tells General Assembly ahead of elections
story_updates.summary: South Sudan remains committed to holding general elections in December to conclude its transition period, the country’s Permanent Representative to the United Nations Cecilia Adout Majok Adeng, told the General Assembly on Monday, calling for all sanctions, including the arms embargo to be lifted.

story_updates.headline: DPR Korea tells UN its nuclear status is ‘irreversible’, rejects outside pressure
story_updates.summary: The Democratic People’s Republic of Korea (DPRK) told the UN General Assembly on Monday that its status as a nuclear-armed State was irreversible, arguing that its military capabilities were necessary to safeguard the country’s sovereignty and maintain peace on the Korean Peninsula.

story_updates.headline: The Takeaway Day 6: General Debate ends with call to turn words into action
story_updates.summary: After six days of speeches from the UN General Assembly podium, one word rose above all others: peace.  This final edition of The Takeaway distils the messages he said reverberated through the Assembly Hall and looks at where the 193-member body goes from here.

story_updates.headline: Yemen escalation fuels fears of further cholera, measles spread
story_updates.summary: Heavy fighting in Yemen is fuelling concerns of an uptick in cholera, measles and other preventable diseases, as overcrowding at displacement sites threatens to overwhelm the limited healthcare services still open.

story_updates.headline: DRC: Early access to care and oxygen decisive for Ebola patients’ survival – WHO
story_updates.summary: In the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), health workers fighting the country’s largest-ever Ebola outbreak are struggling to overcome critical challenges to patient care, the UN World Health Organization (WHO) warned on Tuesday.

story_updates.headline: Security Council LIVE: DRC peace deals fail to halt fighting as Ebola deepens crisis
story_updates.summary: The Security Council met in New York on the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) Tuesday, where clashes between Government forces and M23 rebels continue in the east, despite a series of peace agreements. Ambassadors focused on ceasefire monitoring, rising tensions between the DRC and Rwanda and the country’s worst Ebola outbreak on record, which has killed more than 3,900 people. &...

story_updates.headline: Clean your plate – to reduce food loss and waste
story_updates.summary: Food waste is helping to fuel global warming, one half-eaten sandwich at a time.

story_updates.headline: Funding cuts put 8.3 million refugees at risk of losing vital assistance
story_updates.summary: Haji Mohammad Shafi spent 44 years in Pakistan before he was forced to leave. He sold everything he owned and returned to Afghanistan with his five children, arriving with almost nothing.

story_updates.headline: World News in Brief: Deadly Myanmar strikes as Malaysia begins deportations, new emergency funding released, Gaza and West Bank update
story_updates.summary: The UN chief on Tuesday strongly condemned an airstrike that reportedly killed at least 50 people at a market in Myanmar’s Rakhine state and called for those responsible to be held to account.

story_updates.headline: LIVE: Weighing nuclear risks amid rising tensions and war
story_updates.summary: Amid rising tensions, extreme weather impacts and strikes on nuclear infrastructure in war-torn Iran and Ukraine, UN Member States returned to the core issue of disarmament on Tuesday, closing out the General Assembly’s High-Level Week with calls for greater safeguards.

story_updates.headline: Could a new global panel defuse inequality’s ‘ticking time bomb’?
story_updates.summary: What if the world tackled inequality with the same kind of scientific firepower it has brought to the climate crisis?

story_updates.headline: Lebanon: One in five children goes to bed hungry, says UNICEF
story_updates.summary: Four in five households in Lebanon struggle to afford basic necessities today, with children increasingly going without food, missing school and being pushed into work as conflict compounds years of economic crisis. "I wanted to buy clothes for my children, but I could not. I also wanted to enrol them in school, but I could not afford that either," said one father of four, cited on Wednesday by...

story_updates.headline: Malaysia: UN agency urges safeguards after refugees returned to Myanmar
story_updates.summary: The UN refugee agency, UNHCR, has voiced concern over Malaysia’s decision to return 1,476 people to Myanmar amid an ongoing civil war and a dire human rights and humanitarian situation.

story_updates.headline: Homicides fall as organised crime grows more profitable – and networked
story_updates.summary: Homicide rates are falling across much of the world, but organised crime is on the rise in many regions as criminal networks diversify into trafficking, migrant smuggling, and the exploitation of natural resources, a new UN report launched on Wednesday revealed.

story_updates.headline: Somali families face renewed violence amid worsening hunger crisis
story_updates.summary: Children have been killed and injured in fresh fighting in Baidoa, in Somalia’s South West State, where families were already facing severe hunger and other overlapping crises.

story_updates.headline: World News in Brief: Storm clouds over Gaza, deadly obstacles face Mexican women rights defenders, Latvia booze ban proves lifesaver
story_updates.summary: UN teams are racing to protect families in Gaza from the coming rainy season, but restricted access to land and shortages of critical supplies are hampering the effort, UN Spokesperson Stéphane Dujarric said on Wednesday.

story_updates.headline: Palestinians yearn for ‘a return to normal life,’ says top Middle East peace envoy
story_updates.summary: The UN is continuing efforts to support Palestinians in Gaza amid major challenges to humanitarian access, reconstruction and the restoration of essential services, according to Ramiz Alakbarov, Acting UN Special Coordinator for the Middle East Peace Process.

story_updates.headline: Who gets to shape AI? UN debate centres on power, trust and inclusion
story_updates.summary: Artificial Intelligence or AI – and the technology behind it – is moving fast. The question being asked across the world is who gets a seat at the table deciding how it's used and who gets to benefit.

story_updates.headline: Ebola response faces setback as transit centre burns down in DR Congo camp
story_updates.summary: The enormous challenge of halting the spread of Ebola in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) just became even harder after a key transit centre for patients requiring treatment burned down in Ituri province.

story_updates.headline: Nepal floods threaten jobs and livelihoods beyond disaster zone: ILO
story_updates.summary: The deadly flash floods in northern Nepal have severely disrupted employment and livelihoods, with wider impacts beyond communities that were directly affected, the International Labour Organization (ILO) said in a preliminary assessment released on Thursday.

story_updates.headline: ‘Women are not victims’: Türk calls for women to be at the heart of peace and security
story_updates.summary: Women must be at the centre of efforts to prevent conflict and build lasting peace, UN High Commissioner for Human Rights Volker Türk said on Thursday.

story_updates.headline: World News in Brief: Marshall Islands nuclear legacy, FlyDubai attack condemned, Ukraine update, breast cancer treatment expanded in West…
story_updates.summary: The enduring radioactive legacy of US nuclear bomb testing in the Marshall Islands took centre stage at the Human Rights Council on Thursday.

story_updates.headline: No more execution attempts on Christa Pike: UN rights chief
story_updates.summary: The UN human rights chief and nine independent rights experts on Thursday called on authorities in Tennessee not to pursue any further attempts to execute Christa Pike, saying her case highlights multiple concerns surrounding the death penalty.

story_updates.headline: UN Member States weigh latest Security Council veto, this time on Iran
story_updates.summary: The General Assembly met on Thursday to examine the Security Council’s latest veto, cast by China and Russia over a United States-backed sanctions panel of experts on Iran nuclear facilities.

story_updates.headline: ‘I have not lost my dreams’: Refugee education funding cuts threaten millions
story_updates.summary: A teenage girl who fled war-torn Sudan for neighbouring Egypt and hopes to pursue a technology degree is an example of why countries must ensure that young refugees can continue to learn.

story_updates.headline: Gaza: WHO appeals for massive aid influx ahead of winter
story_updates.summary: Repeated delays in bringing lifesaving medicines, prosthetics and more from Israel into Gaza risk having devastating consequences on Palestinians who urgently need them in the war-torn enclave, the UN World Health Organization (WHO) said on Friday.

story_updates.headline: Escalating fighting in Yemen deepens food security crisis
story_updates.summary: Renewed conflict in Yemen has triggered a surge in hunger that could have consequences in the wider region and beyond, the World Food Programme (WFP) warned on Friday.

story_updates.headline: World News in Brief: Cycle of violence continues in Haiti, seafarer deaths off Somalia, food insecurity in the Middle East
story_updates.summary: Haitians remain in the grip of lethal gang violence as it continues to “adapt and expand”, the UN’s top rights official, Volker Türk, said on Friday.

story_updates.headline: Collective action needed to tackle global information crisis, UN-led dialogue hears
story_updates.summary: Governments, UN entities, civil society, media, academia and the private sector have called for stronger cooperation and practical action to respond to a rapidly changing global information landscape.

story_updates.headline: Ukraine war ‘a human rights catastrophe’ that must end, says Türk
story_updates.summary: The war in Ukraine is a human rights catastrophe that is “growing and intensifying by the week” and threatening an even greater disaster across the region, UN High Commissioner for Human Rights Volker Türk said on Friday.

story_updates.headline: Global life expectancy bounces back to near pre-pandemic levels, WHO says
story_updates.summary: People around the world are living longer again, with global life expectancy almost fully recovered from the disruption of the COVID-19 pandemic, the World Health Organization (WHO) said on Friday.

story_updates.headline: ‘Money alone won’t get us there’: UN steps up aid for 12 forgotten crises
story_updates.summary: Getting aid to people in the world’s most neglected emergencies takes more than money. It takes open roads, open borders and leaders willing to help it reach those in dire need.

story_updates.headline: Uganda’s UN-supported wildlife forensics lab turns ivory seizures into convictions
story_updates.summary: The package originated in Entebbe, Uganda, bound for Cairo, containing 10 kilograms of thumb-sized pieces that could have been either bone or elephant ivory.

story_updates.headline: Rotting food waste emits 5 times more greenhouse gases than planes
story_updates.summary: Rotting food waste is causing up to 10 per cent of total global greenhouse gas emissions – five times more than the entire aviation sector, the UN’s environment agency warned this week.

story_updates.headline: ‘He felt heard’: How a film brought a UN report to life in Xochimilco
story_updates.summary: A documentary drawn from United Nations University research was screened at the COP30 climate conference and film festivals across Europe. Its most important journey, though, was the one back to the Mexico City canals where it was filmed.

story_updates.headline: Beyond the Moon: Space Week around the world
story_updates.summary: Right after the Soviet Union launched Sputnik in 1957, UNOOSA, the UN Office for Outer Space Affairs, was established and has since been monitoring developments across more than 77 successful lunar missions and other journeys while also taking a lead role in the annual World Space Week, which runs from 4 to 10 October.

story_updates.headline: One day behind bars: Students and incarcerated women break prison stigma in Thailand
story_updates.summary: “Your mind follows the thread, one by one, row by row. You know? It’s like meditation. I don’t like machines.”

story_updates.headline: Sudan: Driver killed in aerial attack on aid trucks in South Kordofan
story_updates.summary: The World Food Programme (WFP) has strongly condemned a deadly airstrike on two clearly marked aid trucks in South Kordofan, Sudan, this past weekend.

story_updates.headline: UN upholds housing as a human right on World Habitat Day
story_updates.summary: Representatives from governments, civil society and academia meeting in Muscat, Oman on Monday called for urgent action to address a global housing crisis affecting nearly 3.4 billion people.

story_updates.headline: ICC unseals four arrest warrants over Taliban persecution of women and girls
story_updates.summary: The International Criminal Court (ICC) has made public four arrest warrants against senior Taliban figures, accusing them of persecuting women and girls in Afghanistan, which amounts to a crime against humanity.

story_updates.headline: Extreme heat making pregnancy a ‘new fault line’ in climate crisis
story_updates.summary: Pregnancy and childbirth have become a “new fault line in the global climate crisis” as extreme heat worsens, the head of the UN climate action body (UNFCCC) warned on Monday, calling for maternal and newborn health to be built into countries’ climate plans.

story_updates.headline: Security, sacrifice or opportunity: Visions differ over effective climate action
story_updates.summary: Should the world move away sharply from fossil fuels, or manage a slower, more careful retreat?

story_updates.headline: ‘The clock on AI regulation is ticking’, warns UN rights chief
story_updates.summary: The world is running out of time to put guardrails on artificial intelligence, UN High Commissioner for Human Rights Volker Türk warned Monday, as a “ruthless race” between companies and countries raises concerns about human safety and even humanity’s survival.

story_updates.headline: When streets become pharmacies: Booming illicit markets in Central Africa
story_updates.summary: Antibiotics, malaria treatments, painkillers, opioids. More than 250 tonnes of medical products were seized over six years in Central Africa. Behind those numbers is an illicit market that thrives not simply despite the region’s fragile health systems, but in part because of them.

story_updates.headline: ‘Ebola takes the people children depend on’: UNICEF
story_updates.summary: The Ebola outbreak in the eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) is robbing children of their loved ones – with some succumbing to the deadly disease themselves – the UN Children’s Fund (UNICEF) reported on Tuesday.

story_updates.headline: In Islamabad, Guterres calls for end to US-Iran conflict
story_updates.summary: The UN Secretary-General appealed on Tuesday for an end to the United States-Iran war and the toll it has taken on global trade, as he began an official visit to Pakistan.

story_updates.headline: Testing and monitoring underway in suspected Russia plague death
story_updates.summary: The death of a lab worker in Russia’s Siberia region has sparked concerns over a possible plague case, the UN World Health Organization (WHO) said on Tuesday, adding that it was following the situation closely.

story_updates.headline: Djibouti faces ‘overlapping emergencies’ as Yemen’s refugee exodus continues
story_updates.summary: Djibouti is facing “overlapping emergencies” as refugees fleeing the conflict in Yemen arrive on its shores while migrants continue to travel in the opposite direction, the UN migration agency (IOM) warned on Tuesday.

story_updates.headline: From drought to deluge: ‘Super’ El Niño’s expanding reach
story_updates.summary: Across Papua New Guinea, water sources are drying up, crops are failing and food prices are rising months before the worst agricultural impacts are expected. Behind those warning signs is an El Niño whose Pacific Ocean temperatures have already surpassed the equivalent measurements during the historic 1997 and 2015 events – part of an unfolding climate pattern being dubbed a “Super El Niño” by...

story_updates.headline: ‘Rocket revolution’ opens access to space
story_updates.summary: For a long time, launching something beyond Earth was reserved for a relatively small number of national space programmes. That is changing.

story_updates.headline: Israeli demolition in East Jerusalem displaces 69 Palestinians
story_updates.summary: Sixty-nine Palestinians – more than half of them children – were displaced on Tuesday after Israeli authorities green lit the demolition of their residential building in the At Tur area of East Jerusalem, the UN aid coordination office (OCHA) has reported.

story_updates.headline: WHO releases first global guidelines on child obesity as cases surge
story_updates.summary: Child and adolescent obesity has quadrupled since 1990, rising from two per cent to around eight per cent of youngsters in the five-to-19 age group, according to the UN World Health Organization (WHO).

story_updates.headline: Critical funding gap threatens health response in Yemen
story_updates.summary: The World Health Organization (WHO) warned that significantly more resources are required to scale up its response in Yemen amid escalating conflict and rising needs.

story_updates.headline: Kenya races to trace all contacts after first Ebola death, WHO official says
story_updates.summary: Kenya’s first Ebola death has triggered a race to trace everyone the victim came into contact with, as the United Nations and partners provide full support, the World Health Organization’s (WHO) top official in the country has told UN News in her first interview on the case.

story_updates.headline: World News in Brief: Child migrants in Europe, Greenland forced contraception scandal, FAO hunger updates
story_updates.summary: New data on child migrants published on Wednesday highlighted the harrowing treatment many face while travelling to Europe in search of work and shelter.

story_updates.headline: ‘No plague case’ in Siberia, Russia tells WHO as assessments continue
story_updates.summary: Health authorities in Russia say there is “no plague case” in Siberia following reports last week that a lab technician had died of pneumonia of an unknown origin in the region, World Health Organization (WHO) officials said on Wednesday.

story_updates.headline: Ukraine: UN condemns latest attacks and calls for civilian protection
story_updates.summary: The UN Humanitarian Coordinator for Ukraine on Wednesday called for an end to attacks against civilians following further overnight strikes by Russian forces that reportedly killed at least 19 in the Chernihiv Region.

story_updates.headline: Reform, or lose trust: Governments press the UN to reflect the world as it is
story_updates.summary: Can the UN still remain relevant if it still looks and acts like the organization it was when it was formed in 1945? The debate over UN reform at the General Assembly in New York last month produced a striking common refrain from a diverse range of Member States.

story_updates.headline: Myanmar: Poverty deepens as families face multiple shocks with limited resources
story_updates.summary: Years of conflict, displacement, economic disruption and climate shocks in Myanmar have led to the “simultaneous collapse” of shelter, healthcare, schooling and livelihoods affecting millions of people, the UN Development Programme (UNDP) said in a report issued on Thursday.

story_updates.headline: Afghanistan: Women face fresh dress code arrests amid record refugee returns
story_updates.summary: Afghan women and girls are being arrested, detained and threatened with arrest by Taliban authorities, the UN warned on Thursday as record numbers of returnees struggle to rebuild their lives back home.

story_updates.headline: ‘Age must never diminish rights,’ UN independent expert warns
story_updates.summary: Older women around the world face violence, exploitation and neglect, yet remain largely invisible in the laws, policies, data and services designed to protect women overall, a UN independent human rights expert said on Thursday.

story_updates.headline: UN rights chief: Legacy of slavery and colonialism is still fuelling racism
story_updates.summary: The legacy of enslavement and colonialism continues to shape the lives of Africans and people of African descent, UN human rights chief Volker Türk said on Thursday, calling for urgent action to deliver reparatory justice beyond financial compensation.

story_updates.headline: ‘Overshoot is not a reason to surrender’: UN calls for accelerated climate action ahead of COP31 summit
story_updates.summary: As world leaders prepare for November’s major COP31 climate summit in Türkiye, record-breaking heat, devastating floods and an unprecedented El Niño climate pattern are making global climate action ever more urgent.

story_updates.headline: Darfur: Healthcare needs outstrip resources as Security Council extends Sudan sanctions
story_updates.summary: More than 700,000 displaced people in Tawila, in Sudan’s war-ravaged Darfur region, face severe shortages of healthcare, food, water and protection, the UN World Health Organization (WHO) warned on Thursday as it called for an urgent increase in resources.

story_updates.headline: World News in Brief: Russian attacks continue in Ukraine, Gazans shelter in flood-prone areas, keeping sight of eye health
story_updates.summary: UN human rights chief Volker Türk said on Thursday he was appalled by a wave of attacks that have killed civilians across Ukraine over the past four days.

story_updates.headline: Former UN human rights chief Navi Pillay awarded Nobel Peace Prize
story_updates.summary: South African jurist and former UN High Commissioner for Human Rights Navi Pillay was on Friday announced as the winner of the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize.

story_updates.headline: Security Council LIVE: Yemen has fallen back into full-scale war, warns UN envoy
story_updates.summary: The Security Council met to discuss the crisis in Yemen Friday, where a Houthi offensive launched in September has sharply escalated the 12-year-long war for control of the country and spillover from the US-Iran war has provoked a new displacement crisis. Live coverage below and for full meetings updates, go here.

story_updates.headline: Amid heartache of Nepal flooding disaster, fear remains
story_updates.summary: Six weeks after Nepal’s deadly flooding disaster, communities are still struggling to rebuild their lives, but they will need sustained help as global warming increases the risk of another Himalayan catastrophe, the UN Children’s Fund (UNICEF) said on Friday.

story_updates.headline: Livestreaming US execution would breach prohibition of torture, UN rights office warns
story_updates.summary: The UN human rights office (OHCHR) on Friday warned that livestreaming a planned execution by firing squad in the United States would amount to a public execution and breach the absolute prohibition on torture.

story_updates.headline: World News in Brief: ‘Horrific’ attack in Sudan, Israeli incursions in Syria intensify, most women and girls homeless in Gaza
story_updates.summary: A suspected drone strike has left at least 40 dead in Sudan’s Blue Nile State – near the Ethiopian border - according to initial reports from the ground, according to UN Spokesperson Stéphane Dujarric. Most of the casualties were women and girls.

story_updates.headline: UN chief ‘gravely concerned’ by renewed fighting in northern Ethiopia, warns against escalation
story_updates.summary: UN Secretary-General António Guterres has called for an immediate end to the renewed fighting in northern Ethiopia, saying he is deeply worried by reports that Eritrean forces are present in the country.

story_updates.headline: India: UN rights office urges release of ‘arbitrarily detained’ protesters
story_updates.summary: The UN human rights office (OHCHR) has voiced concern over reports of mass detentions in India of demonstrators, protest leaders, civil society members, lawyers and journalists, before and during large-scale protests in Delhi on Saturday.

story_updates.headline: Sustaining livelihoods amid crisis in Gaza
story_updates.summary: Nidaa, Hanaa and Hanin have different stories, but share a common thread: the determination to build something of their own and keep it going despite extraordinary challenges facing them in war-ravaged Gaza.

story_updates.headline: ‘These attacks must cease immediately’: Guterres condemns deadly Houthi strike on Riyadh airport
story_updates.summary: UN Secretary-General António Guterres has condemned a Houthi missile attack on Riyadh’s main airport that Saudi authorities say killed 12 people and wounded more than 300.

story_updates.headline: Djibouti shipwreck: Death toll rises to 139 as 84 remain missing
story_updates.summary: At least 139 migrants have died after their boat capsized off Djibouti, with a further 84 people still missing, the UN migration agency (IOM) said on Sunday.

story_updates.headline: Rise in poverty is ‘a wake-up call for the world’, UN development chief says
story_updates.summary: The number of people living in “multidimensional” poverty has risen for the first time in 15 years, reaching 1.2 billion, as families struggle to meet their basic needs.

story_updates.headline: ‘Efficiency has limits’: UNHCR chief warns refugee protection is buckling under cuts
story_updates.summary: The money is running out faster than needs are growing: with 117 million men, women and children now forced from their homes, the UN refugee agency (UNHCR) has received just $3 billion of the $8.5 billion it needs this year – and its chief, Barham Salih, warns that the global support system for asylum-seekers risks buckling.

story_updates.headline: UN aid operation underway in Nepal following fresh floods
story_updates.summary: The United Nations has rushed to assist Nepal following new flash floods in the central Gorkha district on Sunday that swept away homes and bridges just weeks after catastrophic flooding in the north.

story_updates.headline: Sudan: Drought and war push Darfur and Kordofan towards famine
story_updates.summary: The risk of famine is growing in parts of Sudan already torn apart by war, as a severe El Niño drought makes life even harder in Greater Darfur and Greater Kordofan, the UN-backed global hunger monitor warned on Monday.

story_updates.headline: Security Council LIVE: Syria’s fragile transition – economic strain, Israeli incursions and progress towards elections
story_updates.summary: The Security Council met to debate Syria's thorny transition Monday as it faces pressure on several fronts. Economic hardship is fuelling unrest, Israeli incursions continue in the south and sectarian tensions persist in Sweida, even as Damascus reports progress on its chemical weapons programme and talks about future elections. Millions, meanwhile, remain displaced. Follow live below and go he...

story_updates.headline: Colombia peace deal must endure as insecurity grows, Security Council hears
story_updates.summary: Nearly 10 years after Colombia signed a historic peace agreement to end a decades-long insurgency, the deal is under strain from growing insecurity – and the UN’s top official in the country says it cannot be allowed to falter.

story_updates.headline: General Assembly adopts pandemic declaration, but not by consensus
story_updates.summary: The General Assembly on Monday adopted a political declaration on pandemic prevention, preparedness and response, by 153 in favour to three against (Argentina, Israel and United States) with two abstentions (New Zealand and Paraguay).

story_updates.headline: Global action to end violence against children is lagging behind risks: UN expert
story_updates.summary: The UN Special Representative on Violence Against Children has called for stronger global action to protect boys and girls caught up in a growing number of crises, as current efforts fall short.

story_updates.headline: Disasters cost $228 billion in housing losses every year
story_updates.summary: $228 billion is a staggering amount of money to find, but that’s exactly what communities around the world are faced with every year, to rebuild housing after disaster strikes.

story_updates.headline: Ukraine: Residents killed and dozens injured in attacks on Kharkiv and Kyiv
story_updates.summary: Russian attacks in recent days on on Ukraine’s two largest cities have again killed and injured civilians, damaged homes and civilian infrastructure, the UN aid coordination office (OCHA) said on Tuesday.

story_updates.headline: ‘Need for UN has never been greater,’ UN chief says, proposing slimmer $3.3 billion budget for 2027
story_updates.summary: Amid climate disruption, an AI revolution, war and growing hunger, “the need for the United Nations has never been greater,” Secretary-General António Guterres said on Tuesday, presenting a $3.3 billion programme budget proposal for next year – a cut of $40.8 million.

story_updates.headline: World News in Brief: West African migrant crossings, Argentina takes UK to maritime tribunal, farming in Gaza, mental health update
story_updates.summary: Fewer people from West Africa are reaching Europe by sea, but the journey has not become safer, the UN migration agency (IOM) said on Tuesday.

story_updates.headline: 800 million young people face a future without jobs
story_updates.summary: Approximately 800 million young people entering the labour market in developing economies over the coming years will not find jobs unless countries act, the head of the UN Development Programme (UNDP) warned on Tuesday, as the agency launched two initiatives to boost investment and employment.

story_updates.headline: Yemen: Houthi siege, cholera outbreak and aid cuts put civilians in the crosshairs
story_updates.summary: Yemen’s southwestern city of Taiz is facing a “devastating” humanitarian crisis as escalating tensions are dramatically driving up food prices and causing shortages of supplies, the UN Spokesperson said on Tuesday.

story_updates.headline: WHO calls for urgent health action across the Eastern Mediterranean
story_updates.summary: The head of the World Health Organization (WHO) has called for promoting, providing and protecting health in the Eastern Mediterranean region, home to some of the world’s top humanitarian crises such as Sudan, Yemen and the Occupied Palestinian Territory.

story_updates.headline: Yemen: WFP warns of potential ‘humanitarian catastrophe’ as fighting blocks aid delivery
story_updates.summary: Intensifying fighting in Yemen has cut off life-saving assistance to 800,000 people as shifting frontlines, blocked roads and growing insecurity severely restrict access to the city of Taiz and other conflict zones, the UN World Food Programme (WFP) said on Wednesday.

story_updates.headline: Security Council LIVE: Libya in the spotlight amid ‘encouraging progress’
story_updates.summary: Despite progress in the political process in Libya, institutional divisions, economic deterioration and security fragility continue to threaten stability, the UN envoy warned the Security Council on Wednesday, calling on Libyan leaders to overcome their differences to pave the way for national elections.

story_updates.headline: Health workers tackle taboos over drinking with new AI tool
story_updates.summary: A new AI-powered hub for health professionals aims to help identify alcohol-related risks and launch discussions with patients, including the link between drinking and cancer, the World Health Organization (WHO) announced on Wednesday.

story_updates.headline: DR Congo: Cholera cases spike amid fight against Ebola
story_updates.summary: The cholera epidemic continues to spread in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), where more than 125,000 suspected cases and 3,644 suspected deaths were recorded between January 2025 and the end of September 2026, the World Health Organization (WHO) warned on Wednesday.

story_updates.headline: World News in Brief: Gaza braces for winter amid attacks, joint patrols in CAR, 90 cities commit to sustainable development
story_updates.summary: The UN and its partners are stepping up preparations in Gaza for the approaching cold and rainy season, even as attacks affecting civilians continue, the UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) said on Wednesday.

story_updates.headline: Colombia: UN independent experts call for Ecopetrol to provide reparations to victims of armed conflict
story_updates.summary: UN independent experts welcomed on Wednesday a recent landmark corporate accountability ruling involving the Ecopetrol oil company by Colombia’s Special Jurisdiction for Peace, calling for reparations for victims.

story_updates.headline: Haiti sanctions renewed: Starving the gangs of bullets
story_updates.summary: Haiti is living through one of the world’s most acute security crises. Armed gangs control large parts of the capital, Port-au-Prince, and are pushing into rural areas, terrorising communities, killing people, committing rape and other sexual assaults, kidnapping for ransom and extorting individuals and businesses.

story_updates.headline: Security Council LIVE: Deaths, demolitions spike in Gaza, West Bank
story_updates.summary: Amid a rise in lethal Israeli strikes, demolitions and violence in Gaza and the West Bank, the Security Council is holding an open debate on Thursday focusing on the current situation in the Occupied Palestinian Territory.

story_updates.headline: WHO urges faster action to end lead exposure which kills 3.5 million annually
story_updates.summary: Countries must accelerate efforts to prevent lead exposure, which is estimated to cause more than 3.5 million deaths globally each year and affects hundreds of millions of children, the World Health Organization (WHO) said on Thursday.

story_updates.headline: WHO urges vigilance after Kenya confirms second Ebola case
story_updates.summary: The World Health Organization (WHO) continues to support Kenya’s efforts to contain Ebola after a second person tested positive for the Bundibugyo virus, the UN agency’s representative in the country said on Thursday.

story_updates.headline: Ukraine: Critical health supplies destroyed in ongoing Russian attacks
story_updates.summary: Ongoing and deadly Russian attacks across Ukraine are causing serious healthcare disruption, with more than $1.5 million-worth of medicines and supplies destroyed in four separate strikes on warehouses used by the UN there since July.

story_updates.headline: AI, green energy and economic transitions risk leaving vulnerable communities behind, UN warns
story_updates.summary: Rapid transformations – from artificial intelligence and digital technologies to renewable energy and demographic shifts – are reshaping economies worldwide, creating new opportunities but also threatening to deepen socio-economic inequalities, a new UN report warned on Thursday.

story_updates.headline: Afghanistan faces record hunger levels amid rampant rights violations
story_updates.summary: Acute malnutrition and hunger in Afghanistan have reached the highest levels ever recorded, with 15.9 million people facing acute food insecurity and conditions set to worsen in the coming months, according to a global hunger monitor report released on Thursday.

story_updates.headline: The world is waging a ‘war on nature’ as progress on biodiversity targets lags
story_updates.summary: Fewer than half of the national targets set to protect the world’s plants, animals and ecosystems are on track, the UN warns in a new report, days before countries gather in Yerevan, Armenia, for the COP17 biodiversity conference.

story_updates.headline: Could your brain data be used against you? UN calls for limits on neurotechnology
story_updates.summary: Brain signals recorded by a gaming headset or a wellness gadget could one day be used as evidence against you in court, according to a new UN report which warns that neurotechnology is outpacing the laws meant to protect human rights.

story_updates.headline: Guterres urges faster action and financing to stop biodiversity loss
story_updates.summary: The United Nations Secretary-General appealed on Friday for governments, businesses and communities to accelerate efforts to protect biodiversity for future generations and all life on Earth.

story_updates.headline: Gaza: 340 children killed despite ceasefire agreement - UNICEF
story_updates.summary: A little over one year since a ceasefire agreement was announced between Hamas fighters and Israel, more than 340 children have been reported killed and hundreds more injured, the UN Children’s Fund (UNICEF) said on Friday.

story_updates.headline: Security Council LIVE: Sudan’s war spreads as drones and hunger take a deadly toll
story_updates.summary: As drone strikes kill civilians from El Obeid to Blue Nile and famine risk spreads across Darfur and Kordofan, the Security Council meets on Sudan – the world’s largest hunger and displacement crisis. Ambassadors are expected to press yet again for a ceasefire, safe aid access and an end to the weapons flows fuelling the brutal conflict.

story_updates.headline: WHO scales up Ebola readiness in 22 countries across three continents
story_updates.summary: The World Health Organization (WHO) is strengthening Ebola preparedness amid conflict and displacement affecting millions of lives in a region that spans parts of Africa, Asia and Europe.

story_updates.headline: Ukraine: Civilian casualty rates among ‘deadliest’ in years, as energy attacks intensify
story_updates.summary: Civilian casualties in Ukraine remain at record levels, with intensified Russian attacks in September continuing a pattern of harm in 2026 far exceeding previous years, UN human rights monitors in Ukraine said on Friday.

story_updates.headline: As disasters mount, next UN climate summit faces a test of trust
story_updates.summary: Less than a month before the UN climate conference COP31 opens in Antalya, Türkiye, representatives of three successive summit presidencies gathered to address a pressing question: How can the world restore trust in climate action when the consequences of a warming planet are already being felt?

story_updates.headline: COP17: The world has a plan to save nature. Is it working?
story_updates.summary: The UN Secretary-General has called for an end to the “war on nature”. On Monday, governments gathering in Yerevan, Armenia, will have to confront a more practical question: are they doing enough to win the peace and put the world’s biodiversity goals back on track?

story_updates.headline: Flour sacks turned flood barriers: Gaza faces another winter without safe shelter
story_updates.summary: Like many people in the war-ravaged Gaza Strip, Ahmed Al-Omari is preparing for another winter of bitter cold and rain that threatens to cause flooding as families struggle to survive in tattered tents and damaged buildings.

story_updates.headline: Inside the New York ‘time machine’ racing to save a century of sound and film
story_updates.summary: “I tell my kids I work in a time machine,” said Rhony Dostaly. In a basement beneath Lincoln Center, the media preservation engineer rescues moments from the past. “I go back in time, and I grab elements, and I make them available for people today.”

story_updates.headline: Protecting Earth’s fragile biodiversity takes spotlight at Armenia talks
story_updates.summary: Biodiversity losses continue to upend the lives of billions of people whose future prosperity depends on countries taking urgent action to protect our planet, the top UN official leading talks at the UN Biodiversity Conference in Yerevan, said on Monday.

story_updates.headline: Gaza: Funding cuts leave half a million without food assistance
story_updates.summary: Funding shortages have forced the World Food Programme (WFP) to slash assistance to hungry families in the Gaza Strip by roughly one third – a move that will affect some 500,000 people as winter approaches, the UN agency announced on Monday.

story_updates.headline: Guterres honours Indonesian troops who paid ‘ultimate sacrifice’
story_updates.summary: UN Secretary-General António Guterres paid tribute to Indonesian peacekeepers on Monday, laying a wreath in honour of four who recently lost their lives in Lebanon and offering a robust defence of UN peacekeeping in what he called “testing times for peace”.

story_updates.headline: ‘Season of fear’: Escalating Israeli attacks on West Bank olive farmers, deadly strikes on Gaza
story_updates.summary: Israeli attacks on war-torn Gaza over the weekend killed at least six Palestinians, including children, despite a year-old ceasefire agreement. Meanwhile, in the occupied West Bank, settler violence continued through the ongoing olive harvest, with UN independent experts on Monday urging Israel to protect Palestinian farmers.

story_updates.headline: Haiti: Elections on hold as gangs adapt to security crackdown, Security Council hears
story_updates.summary: Armed groups in Haiti are adapting to intensified security operations, stepping up reprisals against civilians and extending their reach into rural areas, the UN warned the Security Council on Monday.

story_updates.headline: Hunger is ‘an avoidable tragedy’ in a world of plenty: Türk
story_updates.summary: More than a quarter of humanity struggles to get enough food, even though the world produces enough for everyone, UN human rights chief Volker Türk said on Monday, blaming injustice and the denial of human rights for hunger in a world of plenty.

story_updates.headline: UN condemns deadly wave of drone strikes in war-torn Sudan
story_updates.summary: Drone strikes killed and injured dozens across Sudan on Monday as the ongoing war continues to cause soaring displacement and hunger.

story_updates.headline: Yemen war continues to force families from homes amid hunger and disease
story_updates.summary: More than 250,000 people have now fled renewed fighting in Yemen, the UN said on Tuesday, citing particular concern for those sheltering in the southwestern city of Taiz and the wider governorate, where access is “essentially blocked”.

story_updates.headline: ‘One step away from famine’: Inside Afghanistan’s hunger crisis
story_updates.summary: Following extreme hunger warnings, a bitter reality is unfolding across Afghanistan: food is available, but remains inaccessible for millions of people.

story_updates.headline: Bangladesh: UNICEF chief calls for an end to child marriage
story_updates.summary: At 14, Bushra faced being married off – until community leaders at a UNICEF-supported child protection hub worked with her father to prevent her from being given away against her will.

story_updates.headline: Sudan conflict: Peace efforts resume to end ‘drone war’ fuelling humanitarian crisis
story_updates.summary: Talks to halt the fighting in Sudan and alleviate the humanitarian crisis there continued in Geneva on Wednesday, where nearly two dozen countries convened to discuss a pathway to a ceasefire and transition to peaceful governance that represents all Sudanese people.

story_updates.headline: Summit in Samarkand, a boon for child wellbeing and health
story_updates.summary: Representatives from across the international community are meeting in Samarkand, Uzbekistan, to ensure that children everywhere can thrive in a world marred by war, climate chaos and other fundamental challenges.

story_updates.headline: Fate unknown of many returned to DPR Korea from China: UN independent experts
story_updates.summary: Three years on from the reported resumption of large-scale forcible returns of nationals of the Democratic People’s Republic of Korea (DPRK) from China, serious concerns persist about their fate, according to a group of Human Rights Council-appointed independent experts.

story_updates.headline: ‘Connect the dots’ between street protests and global turmoil, urges Guterres
story_updates.summary: The international community must combat inequality and stop wars from expanding to ensure a safer world for all, the UN Secretary-General said on Thursday.

story_updates.headline: World News in Brief: Russian attacks intensify, UN team tours West Bank, ‘unlawful’ elderly deaths
story_updates.summary: Long-range Russian attacks across Ukraine are intensifying, including in Kyiv, causing at least 14 civilian deaths and 78 injuries overnight into Thursday, as UN agencies continue to provide aid.

story_updates.headline: Yemen: Deepening concerns for Taiz City as aid is blocked from entering
story_updates.summary: Aid agencies warned on Friday of the fast-developing humanitarian emergency inside Taiz City in Yemen, which has been encircled by de facto Houthi forces fighting government troops along the country’s west coast.

story_updates.headline: West Bank: Guterres alarmed as Israel imposes sweeping closures after deadly Hebron attack
story_updates.summary: The UN said on Friday it was “extremely alarmed” by intensifying violence in the occupied West Bank, as Israel moved to seal off the territory following a deadly attack on its soldiers in Hebron.

story_updates.headline: World News in Brief: Iran nuclear inspections, deadly church attack in Jordan, El Fasher – one year on
story_updates.summary: The head of the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA), Rafael Grossi, called on Friday for a swift return of inspectors to Iran, warning of growing fragility in the global nuclear non-proliferation regime.

story_updates.headline: UN marks 81 years of global cooperation
story_updates.summary: The United Nations celebrates its 81st anniversary on Saturday, highlighting more than eight decades of work to advance peace, human rights and development around the world.

story_updates.headline: Ebola: UN officials condemn killing of nurse in DR Congo
story_updates.summary: The UN’s Ebola coordinator and the head of the World Health Organization (WHO) have deplored the killing of a nurse working to halt the spread of the disease in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC).

story_updates.headline: In Egypt, Guterres warns against Iran-US escalation
story_updates.summary: UN Secretary-General António Guterres called for dialogue and diplomacy to end the war between Iran and the United States in remarks on Monday to journalists in Cairo, Egypt.
